bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑巻第二百一十四

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十】起閼逢閹茂，盡重光大荒落，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 30] From Emao through Guanghuang Dahuangluo; eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 30] From the jiaxu year through the xinyou year—eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳，上-{發}-西京；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jisi, the Emperor set out from the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jisi, Emperor Xuanzong set out from Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，至東都。

translations.literal: on jichou, he reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: on jichou, he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 張九齡自韶州入見，求終喪；

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling came from Shaozhou to have an audience and asked to complete his mourning period;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling came from Shaozhou to have an audience and asked to be allowed to finish mourning for his parent;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，秦州地連震，壞公私屋殆盡，吏民壓死者四千-{餘}-人；

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, Qin Prefecture suffered a succession of earthquakes; public and private buildings were nearly all destroyed, and more than four thousand officials and commoners were crushed to death;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, Qin Prefecture suffered a succession of earthquakes; public and private buildings were nearly all destroyed, and more than four thousand officials and commoners were crushed to death;

sentences.zh: 命左丞相蕭-{嵩}-賑恤。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Left Chancellor Xiao Song to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Left Chancellor Xiao Song to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 方士張果自言有神仙-{術}-，誑人-{云}-堯時爲侍中，-{於}-今數千歳；

translations.literal: The Daoist adept Zhang Guo claimed to possess immortal arts and deceived people by saying he had been a Palace Attendant in the time of Yao and was now several thousand years old;
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist adept Zhang Guo claimed to possess immortal arts and deceived people by saying he had been a Palace Attendant in the time of Yao and was now several thousand years old;

sentences.zh: 多往來恆山中，則天以來，屢-{-{征}-}-不至。

translations.literal: He often traveled about Mount Heng; since the reign of Empress Wu he had been summoned many times but never came.
translations.idiomatic: He often traveled about Mount Heng; since the reign of Empress Wu he had been summoned many times but never came.

sentences.zh: 恆州刺史韋濟-{薦}-之，上遣中書-{舍}-人徐嶠繼璽書迎之。

translations.literal: Heng Prefecture Inspector Wei Ji recommended him, and the Emperor sent Palace Draftsman Xu Qiao with a second imperial letter to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Prefecture Inspector Wei Ji recommended him, and the Emperor sent Palace Draftsman Xu Qiao with a second imperial letter to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，至東都，肩輿入宮，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: On gengyin he reached the Eastern Capital, was carried into the palace in a palanquin, and received very generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he reached Luoyang, was carried into the palace in a palanquin, and received very generous favor.

sentences.zh: 張九齡請不禁鑄錢，三月，庚辰，敕百官議之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling asked that private coinage not be forbidden; in the third month, on gengchen, the Emperor ordered the hundred officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling asked that private coinage not be forbidden; in the third month, on gengchen, the Emperor ordered the hundred officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿等皆曰：「一啓此門，恐小人棄農逐利，而濫惡更甚。」

translations.literal: Pei Yaoji and the others all said: "Once this gate is opened, I fear petty men will abandon farming to pursue profit, and debased coin will grow worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoji and the others all said: "Once this gate is opened, I fear petty men will abandon farming to pursue profit, and debased coin will grow worse still.

sentences.zh: 秘書監崔沔曰：「若稅銅折役，則官冶可成，計估度庸，則私鑄無利，易而可久，簡而難誣。

translations.literal: Secretary Supervisor Cui Hao said: "If copper is taxed and corvée substituted, then government minting can succeed; if costs are estimated and corvée assessed, then private casting will be unprofitable—easy to maintain long, simple and hard to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Supervisor Cui Hao said: "If copper is taxed and corvée substituted, then government minting can succeed; if costs are estimated and corvée assessed, then private casting will be unprofitable—easy to maintain long, simple and hard to deceive.

sentences.zh: 且夫錢之爲物，貴以通貨，利不在多，何待私鑄然-{後}-足用也！」

translations.literal: Moreover, as a commodity money exists to circulate goods; the benefit lies not in abundance—why wait for private casting before there is enough!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, money exists to circulate goods; the benefit lies not in abundance—why wait for private casting before there is enough!

sentences.zh: 右監門録事參軍劉秩曰：「夫人富則不可以賞勸，貧則不可以威禁，若許其私鑄，貧者必不能爲之；

translations.literal: Right Supervisory Gate Clerk Liu Zhi said: "When men are rich, rewards cannot encourage them; when poor, punishments cannot restrain them. If private casting is permitted, the poor certainly cannot do it;
translations.idiomatic: Right Supervisory Gate Clerk Liu Zhi said: "When men are rich, rewards cannot encourage them; when poor, punishments cannot restrain them. If private casting is permitted, the poor certainly cannot do it;

sentences.zh: 臣恐貧者益貧而役-{於}-富，富者益富而逞其欲。

translations.literal: I fear the poor will grow poorer while serving the rich, and the rich will grow richer while indulging their desires.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the poor will grow poorer while serving the rich, and the rich will grow richer while indulging their desires.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝時，呉王濞富埒天子，鑄錢所致也。」

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, King Liu Pi of Wu was as wealthy as the Son of Heaven—this came of casting coin."
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, King Liu Pi of Wu was as wealthy as the Son of Heaven—this came of casting coin.

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 秩，子玄之子也。

translations.literal: Zhi was the son of Liu Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was the son of Liu Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬辰，以朔方節度使信安王禕兼關内道採訪處置使，增領涇、原等十二州。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renchen, Prince Xin'an Li Yi was made Shuo-fang Military Commissioner and concurrently Guannei Circuit Investigation and Disposition Commissioner, with twelve additional prefectures including Jing and Yuan added to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renchen, Prince Xin'an Li Yi was made Shuo-fang Military Commissioner and concurrently Guannei Circuit Investigation and Disposition Commissioner, with twelve additional prefectures including Jing and Yuan added to his command.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎李林甫，柔佞多狡數，深結宦官及妃嬪家，侍候上動靜，無不知之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was supple, sycophantic, and full of crafty schemes; he forged deep ties with eunuchs and the households of imperial consorts, attending to the Emperor's every move so that nothing escaped his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was supple, sycophantic, and full of crafty schemes; he forged deep ties with eunuchs and the households of imperial consorts, attending to the Emperor's every move so that nothing escaped his knowledge.

sentences.zh: 由是毎奏對，常稱旨，上悅之。

translations.literal: Because of this, whenever he memorialized or answered in audience he usually hit the mark with the Emperor's wishes, and the Emperor was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, whenever he memorialized or answered in audience he usually hit the mark with the Emperor's wishes, and the Emperor was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 時武惠妃寵幸傾-{後}-宮，生壽王淸，諸子莫得爲比，太子浸疎薄。

translations.literal: At the time Consort Wu Huifei's favor eclipsed the entire inner palace; she bore Prince Shou, Qing, and none of the other princes could compare, while the Crown Prince grew gradually estranged.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Consort Wu Huifei's favor eclipsed the entire inner palace; she bore Prince Shou, Li Qing, and none of the other princes could compare, while the Crown Prince grew gradually estranged.

sentences.zh: 林甫乃因宦官言-{於}-惠妃，-{願}-盡力保護壽王；

translations.literal: Linfu then spoke through eunuchs to Huifei, expressing his wish to do all he could to protect Prince Shou;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu then spoke through eunuchs to Huifei, expressing his wish to do all he could to protect Prince Shou;

sentences.zh: 惠妃德之，陰爲内助，由是擢黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Huifei was grateful to him and secretly aided him within; because of this he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei was grateful to him and secretly aided him within; because of this he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊子，以裴耀卿爲侍中，張九齡爲中書令，林甫爲禮部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Pei Yaoji was made Palace Attendant, Zhang Jiuling was made Director of the Secretariat, and Linfu was made Minister of Rites and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Pei Yaoji was made Palace Attendant, Zhang Jiuling was made Director of the Secretariat, and Linfu was made Minister of Rites and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the third rank.

sentences.zh: 上-{種}-麥-{於}-苑中，帥太子以來親往芟之，謂曰：「此所以-{薦}-宗廟，故不敢不親，且欲使汝曹知稼穡艱難耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor planted wheat in the palace park and led the Crown Prince to go in person to reap it, saying: "This is to supply the ancestral temple, so I dare not be uninvolved; moreover I wish you to know how hard fieldwork is."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor planted wheat in the palace park and led the Crown Prince to go in person to reap it, saying: "This is to supply the ancestral temple, so I dare not be uninvolved; moreover I wish you to know how hard fieldwork is.

sentences.zh: 又遍以賜侍臣曰：「比遣人視田中稼，多不得實，故自-{種}-以觀之。」

translations.literal: He also distributed it widely to attending ministers, saying: "When I sent men to inspect the crops in the fields, they often did not report the truth, so I planted it myself to see."
translations.idiomatic: He also distributed it widely to attending ministers, saying: "When I sent men to inspect the crops in the fields, they often did not report the truth, so I planted it myself to see."

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，幽州節度使張守珪大破契丹，遣使獻捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renchen, Shuo-fang Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui inflicted a great defeat on the Khitan and sent envoys to present a victory report.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen, Shuo-fang Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui inflicted a great defeat on the Khitan and sent envoys to present a victory report.

sentences.zh: 薛王業疾病，上憂之，容-{發}-爲變。

translations.literal: Prince Xue, Ye, fell ill; the Emperor worried over him and his countenance changed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xue, Li Ye, fell ill; the Emperor worried over him and his countenance changed.

sentences.zh: 七月，己巳，薨，贈謚惠宣太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on jisi, Ye died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Huixuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jisi, Li Ye died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Huixuan.

sentences.zh: 上以裴耀卿爲江淮、河南轉運使，-{於}-河口置輸塲。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Pei Yaoji Commissioner for Transport on the Jiang-Huai and Henan circuits and established a transshipment depot at Hekou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Pei Yaoji Commissioner for Transport on the Jiang-Huai and Henan circuits and established a transshipment depot at Hekou.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，-{於}-輸塲東置河陰倉，西置柏崖倉，三門東置集津倉，西置鹽倉；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, east of the transshipment depot he established Heyin Granary, to the west Bayai Granary, east of Sanmen Pass Jijin Granary, and to the west Salt Granary;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, east of the transshipment depot he established Heyin Granary, to the west Bayai Granary, east of Sanmen Pass Jijin Granary, and to the west Salt Granary;

sentences.zh: 鑿漕渠十八-{里}-，以避三門之險。

translations.literal: he cut an eighteen-li canal to avoid the peril of Sanmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: he cut an eighteen-li canal to avoid the peril of Sanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 先是，舟運江、淮之米至東都含嘉倉，僦車陸運，三百-{里}-至陝，率兩斛用十錢。

translations.literal: Previously, grain boats from the Jiang and Huai had been shipped to the Hejia Granary at the Eastern Capital, then hired carts for overland transport three hundred li to Shaan, at a rate of ten cash for every two hu.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, grain boats from the Jiang and Huai had been shipped to the Hejia Granary at Luoyang, then hired carts for overland transport three hundred li to Shaan, at a rate of ten cash for every two hu.

sentences.zh: 耀卿令江、淮舟運悉輸河陰倉，更用河舟運至含嘉倉及太原倉，自太原倉入渭輸關中，凡三歳，運米七百萬斛，省僦車錢三十萬緡。

translations.literal: Yaoji ordered all Jiang-Huai boat transport to unload at Heyin Granary, then used river boats to ship to Hejia Granary and Taiyuan Granary; from Taiyuan Granary grain entered the Wei to supply Guanzhong. In all three years seven million hu of rice were moved, saving three hundred thousand strings in cart hire.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoji ordered all Jiang-Huai boat transport to unload at Heyin Granary, then used river boats to ship to Hejia Granary and Taiyuan Granary; from Taiyuan Granary grain entered the Wei to supply Guanzhong. In all three years seven million hu of rice were moved, saving three hundred thousand strings in cart hire.

sentences.zh: 或説耀卿獻所省錢，耀卿曰：「此公家贏縮之利耳，奈何以之市寵乎！」

translations.literal: Someone urged Yaoji to present the money saved; Yaoji said: "This is merely the state's surplus or shortfall in profit—how could I use it to buy favor!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Yaoji to present the money saved; Yaoji said: "This is merely the state's surplus or shortfall in profit—how could I use it to buy favor!

sentences.zh: 悉奏以爲市糴錢。

translations.literal: He memorialized it all to be used as funds for market purchases of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized it all to be used as funds for market purchases of grain.

sentences.zh: 張果固請歸恆山，-{制}-以爲銀靑光祿大夫，號通玄先生，厚賜而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhang Guo firmly asked to return to Mount Heng; by imperial order he was made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of the Palace, styled Master Tongxuan, richly rewarded and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guo firmly asked to return to Mount Heng; by imperial order he was made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of the Palace, styled Master Tongxuan, richly rewarded and sent away.

sentences.zh: -{後}-卒，好異者奏以爲屍解；

translations.literal: Later he died; enthusiasts of the strange memorialized that he had undergone corpse liberation;
translations.idiomatic: Later he died; enthusiasts of the strange memorialized that he had undergone corpse liberation;

sentences.zh: 上由是頗信神仙。

translations.literal: because of this the Emperor came to believe strongly in immortals.
translations.idiomatic: because of this the Emperor came to believe strongly in immortals.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，戊子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the wuzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on the wuzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，幽州節度使張守珪斬契丹王屈烈及可突-{干}-，傳首。

translations.literal: On yisi, You Prefecture Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui beheaded the Khitan king Qu Lie and Ketugan and sent their heads.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, You Prefecture Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui beheaded the Khitan king Qu Lie and Ketugan and sent their heads.

sentences.zh: 時可突-{干}-連年爲邊患，趙含章、薛楚玉皆不能討。

translations.literal: At the time Ketugan had for years been a border menace; Zhao Hanzhang and Xue Chuyu had both been unable to subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ketugan had for years been a border menace; Zhao Hanzhang and Xue Chuyu had both been unable to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 守珪到官，屢撃破之。

translations.literal: When Shougui took office he repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shougui took office he repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 可突-{干}-困迫，遣使詐降，守珪使管記王悔就撫之。

translations.literal: Ketugan, hard pressed, sent envoys to feign surrender; Shougui sent Recorder Wang Hui to go and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Ketugan, hard pressed, sent envoys to feign surrender; Shougui sent Recorder Wang Hui to go and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 悔至其牙帳，察契丹上下初無降意，但稍徙營帳近西北，密遣人引突厥，謀殺悔以叛；

translations.literal: When Hui reached their royal tent he observed that high and low among the Khitan at first had no intent to surrender, but only gradually moved their camps somewhat toward the northwest, secretly sending men to bring in the Turks and plotting to kill Hui and rebel;
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached their royal tent he observed that high and low among the Khitan at first had no intent to surrender, but only gradually moved their camps somewhat toward the northwest, secretly sending men to bring in the Turks and plotting to kill Hui and rebel;

sentences.zh: 悔知之。

translations.literal: Hui learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui learned of it.

sentences.zh: 牙官李過折與可突-{干}-分典兵馬，爭權不-{葉}-，悔説過折使圖之。

translations.literal: Yamen officer Li Guozhe and Ketugan each commanded troops and horses and contended for power without yielding; Hui persuaded Guozhe to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen officer Li Guozhe and Ketugan each commanded troops and horses and contended for power without yielding; Hui persuaded Guozhe to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 過折夜勒兵斬屈烈及可突-{干}-，盡誅其黨，帥-{餘}-衆來降。

translations.literal: Guozhe led troops by night and beheaded Qu Lie and Ketugan, put their entire faction to the sword, and led the remaining multitude to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhe led troops by night and beheaded Qu Lie and Ketugan, put their entire faction to the sword, and led the remaining multitude to surrender.

sentences.zh: 守珪出師紫蒙州，大閲以鎭撫之，梟屈烈、可突-{干}-首-{於}-天津之南。

translations.literal: Shougui marched out to Zimeng Prefecture and held a grand review to pacify them, exposing the heads of Qu Lie and Ketugan south of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui marched out to Zimeng Prefecture and held a grand review to pacify them, exposing the heads of Qu Lie and Ketugan south of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 突厥毘伽可汗爲其大臣梅録啜所毒，未死，討誅梅録啜及其族黨。

translations.literal: The Türk Qapaghan Khaghan was poisoned by his minister Meiluchuo; before he died he punished and executed Meiluchuo and his clan faction.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk Qapaghan Khaghan was poisoned by his minister Meiluchuo; before he died he punished and executed Meiluchuo and his clan faction.

sentences.zh: 既卒，子伊然可汗立。

translations.literal: When he had died, his son Yiran Khaghan was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: When he had died, his son Yiran Khaghan was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，弟登利可汗立。

translations.literal: Soon after he too died, and his younger brother Dengli Khaghan was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he too died, and his younger brother Dengli Khaghan was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，來告喪。

translations.literal: On gengxu envoys came to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu envoys came to announce the mourning.

sentences.zh: 禁京城丐者，置病坊以廩之。

translations.literal: Beggars in the capital were forbidden; sick wards were established to supply them from the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Beggars in the capital were forbidden; sick wards were established to supply them from the granaries.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，契丹知兵馬中郎李過折來獻捷；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Khitan Director of Military Affairs Central-Commander Li Guozhe came to present a victory report;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Khitan Director of Military Affairs Central-Commander Li Guozhe came to present a victory report;

sentences.zh: -{制}-以過折爲北平王，檢校-{松}-漠州都督。

translations.literal: by imperial order Guozhe was made Prince of Beiping and Acting Military Commissioner of Songmo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: by imperial order Guozhe was made Prince of Beiping and Acting Military Commissioner of Songmo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上耕藉田，九推乃止；

translations.literal: On yihai the Emperor plowed the sacred field; after nine furrows he stopped;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Emperor plowed the sacred field; after nine furrows he stopped;

sentences.zh: 公卿以下皆終畝。

translations.literal: the dukes and ministers below all finished their allotted acres.
translations.idiomatic: the dukes and ministers below all finished their allotted acres.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，都城酺三日。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty for the realm; the capital held feasting for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty for the realm; the capital held feasting for three days.

sentences.zh: 上-{御}-五鳳樓酺宴，觀者喧隘，樂不得奏，金吾白梃如雨，不能遏；

translations.literal: The Emperor held a feast at Wufeng Tower; the spectators were noisy and crowded, music could not be played, and the Golden Guard's white clubs rained down yet could not hold them back;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held a feast at Wufeng Tower; the spectators were noisy and crowded, music could not be played, and the Golden Guard's white clubs rained down yet could not hold them back;

sentences.zh: 上患之。

translations.literal: the Emperor was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor was troubled by it.

sentences.zh: 髙力士奏河南丞嚴安之爲理嚴，爲人所畏，請使止之；

translations.literal: Gao Lishi memorialized that Henan Assistant Magistrate Yan Anzhi was strict in judgment and feared by men, and asked that he be sent to stop it;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi memorialized that Henan Assistant Magistrate Yan Anzhi was strict in judgment and feared by men, and asked that he be sent to stop it;

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 安之至，以手板繞塲畫地曰：「犯此者死！」

translations.literal: When Anzhi arrived he drew a line on the ground with his tablet and said: "Whoever crosses this dies!"
translations.idiomatic: When Anzhi arrived he drew a line on the ground with his tablet and said: "Whoever crosses this dies!

sentences.zh: -{於}-是盡三日，人指其畫以相戒，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: Thereupon for the full three days people pointed to his line to warn one another, and none dared violate it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon for the full three days people pointed to his line to warn one another, and none dared violate it.

sentences.zh: 時命三百-{里}-内刺史、縣令各帥所部音樂集-{於}-樓下，各較勝負。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor ordered prefects and magistrates within three hundred li each to lead their local musicians to assemble below the tower and compete for superiority.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Emperor ordered prefects and magistrates within three hundred li each to lead their local musicians to assemble below the tower and compete for superiority.

sentences.zh: 懷州刺史上車載樂工數百，皆衣文繡，服箱之牛皆爲虎豹犀象之狀。

translations.literal: The prefect of Huai Prefecture came in a carriage loaded with several hundred musicians, all dressed in patterned brocade, and the oxen pulling the carts were caparisoned to look like tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Huai Prefecture came in a carriage loaded with several hundred musicians, all dressed in patterned brocade, and the oxen pulling the carts were caparisoned to look like tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants.

sentences.zh: 魯山令元德秀惟遣樂工數人，連袂歌《-{於}-□》。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Lushan, Yuan Dexiu, sent only a few musicians who sang in linked sleeves the song "Yu [character lost]."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Lushan, Yuan Dexiu, sent only a few musicians who sang in linked sleeves the song "Yu [character lost]."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「懷州之人，其塗炭乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Are the people of Huai Prefecture being tormented in a cauldron!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Are the people of Huai Prefecture being tormented in a cauldron!

sentences.zh: 立以刺史爲散官。

translations.literal: He immediately demoted the prefect to an honorary office.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately demoted the prefect to an honorary office.

sentences.zh: 德秀性介潔質-{樸}-，士大夫皆服其髙。

translations.literal: Dexiu's nature was upright, frugal, and plain; scholar-officials all admired his loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dexiu was upright, frugal, and unadorned; scholar-officials all admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 上美張守珪之功，欲以爲相，張九齡諫曰：「宰相者，代天理物，非賞功之官也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor admired Zhang Shougui's achievement and wished to make him chancellor; Zhang Jiuling remonstrated, saying: "The chancellor is one who on behalf of Heaven orders the myriad things—it is not an office for rewarding merit."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired Zhang Shougui's achievement and wished to make him chancellor; Zhang Jiuling remonstrated, saying: "The chancellor is one who on behalf of Heaven orders the myriad things—it is not an office for rewarding merit.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「假以其名而不使任其職，可乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Suppose I lend him the title but do not let him bear the duties—would that do?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Suppose I lend him the title but do not let him bear the duties—would that do?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不可。

translations.literal: He replied: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 惟名與器不可以假人，君之所司也。

translations.literal: Titles and regalia must not be lent to others—this is what the ruler oversees.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and regalia must not be lent to others—this is what the ruler oversees.

sentences.zh: 且守珪-{才}-破契丹，陛下即以爲宰相；

translations.literal: Moreover Shougui has only just defeated the Khitan; Your Majesty would at once make him chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shougui has only just defeated the Khitan; Your Majesty would at once make him chancellor;

sentences.zh: 若盡滅奚、厥，將以何官賞之？」

translations.literal: if he utterly destroys the Xi and the Mohe, with what office will you reward him?"
translations.idiomatic: if he utterly destroys the Xi and the Mohe, with what office will you reward him?

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 二月，守珪詣東都獻捷，拜右羽林大將軍，兼-{御}-史大夫，賜二子官，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: In the second month Shougui came to the Eastern Capital to present his victory; he was appointed General of the Right Feathered Forest, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, his two sons were granted office, and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Shougui came to Luoyang to present his victory; he was appointed General of the Right Feathered Forest, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, his two sons were granted office, and rewards were very generous.

sentences.zh: 初，殿中侍-{御}-史楊汪既殺張審素，更名萬頃。

translations.literal: Earlier, Palace Attendant Censor Yang Wang had killed Zhang Shensu and changed his name to Wanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Attendant Censor Yang Wang had killed Zhang Shensu and changed his name to Wanqing.

sentences.zh: 審素二子□、琇皆幼，坐流嶺表；

translations.literal: Shensu's two sons [name lost] and Xiu were both young and were sentenced to exile in Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Shensu's two sons [name lost] and Zhang Xiu were both young and were sentenced to exile in Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 尋逃歸，謀伺便-{復}-仇。

translations.literal: soon they fled back and plotted to seize an opportunity for revenge.
translations.idiomatic: soon they fled back and plotted to seize an opportunity for revenge.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁卯，手殺萬頃-{於}-都城。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingmao, they personally killed Wanqing in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao, they personally killed Wanqing in the capital.

sentences.zh: -{系}-表-{於}-斧，言父冤狀，欲之江外殺與萬頃同謀陷其父者。

translations.literal: They bound a petition to an axe stating their father's grievance and intended to go beyond the river to kill those who had conspired with Wanqing to frame their father.
translations.idiomatic: They bound a petition to an axe stating their father's grievance and intended to go beyond the river to kill those who had conspired with Wanqing to frame their father.

sentences.zh: 至汜水，爲有司所得。

translations.literal: When they reached Sishui they were seized by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Sishui they were seized by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 議者多言二子父死非罪，稚年孝烈，能-{復}-父仇，宜加矜宥；

translations.literal: Those who deliberated mostly said the two sons' father had died without guilt; in their tender years they were filial and fierce and could avenge their father—they should be shown leniency;
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberated mostly said the two sons' father had died without guilt; in their tender years they were filial and fierce and could avenge their father—they should be shown leniency;

sentences.zh: 張九齡亦欲活之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling also wished to spare their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling also wished to spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿、李林甫以爲如此壞國法，上亦以爲然，謂九齡曰：「孝子之情，義不顧死；

translations.literal: Pei Yaoji and Li Linfu held that to do so would ruin the laws of the state; the Emperor also thought so, and said to Jiuling: "A filial son's feeling is such that he will not regard death;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoji and Li Linfu held that to do so would ruin the laws of the state; the Emperor also thought so, and said to Jiuling: "A filial son's feeling is such that he will not regard death;

sentences.zh: 然殺人而赦之，此塗不可啓也。」

translations.literal: yet to kill a man and then pardon him—this path must not be opened."
translations.idiomatic: yet to kill a man and then pardon him—this path must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 乃下敕曰：「國家設法，期-{於}-止殺。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict: "The state establishes laws expecting thereby to stop killing.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "The state establishes laws expecting thereby to stop killing.

sentences.zh: 各伸爲子之-{志}-，誰非徇孝之人？

translations.literal: If each extends a son's intent, who is not a man bent on filial duty?
translations.idiomatic: If each extends a son's intent, who is not a man bent on filial duty?

sentences.zh: 展轉相仇，何有限極！

translations.literal: Vengeance passed back and forth—what limit could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Vengeance passed back and forth—what limit could there be!

sentences.zh: 咎繇作士，法在必行。

translations.literal: When Gao Yao was Minister of Crime, the law had to be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yao was Minister of Crime, the law had to be enforced.

sentences.zh: 曾參殺人，亦不可恕。

translations.literal: Even if Zeng Shen had killed a man, he could not be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zeng Shen had killed a man, he could not be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 宜付河南府杖殺。」

translations.literal: They are to be handed to Henan Prefecture to be beaten to death."
translations.idiomatic: They are to be handed to Henan Prefecture to be beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 士民皆憐之，爲作哀誄，榜-{於}-衢路。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials and commoners all pitied them and composed mourning eulogies, posting them on the public roads.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials and commoners pitied them, composed mourning eulogies, and posted them along the public roads.

sentences.zh: 市人斂錢葬之-{於}-北邙。

translations.literal: Townsmen collected money and buried them on Mount Beimang.
translations.idiomatic: Townsmen collected money and buried the brothers on Mount Beimang.

sentences.zh: 恐萬頃家-{發}-之，仍爲作疑塚凡數處。

translations.literal: Fearing that Wanqing's family would dig them up, they also built several decoy tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wanqing's kin might exhume the bodies, they also built several decoy tombs.

sentences.zh: 唐初，公主實封止三百戸，中宗時，太平公主至五千戸，率以七丁爲限。

translations.literal: In early Tang, princesses' actual fiefs were limited to three hundred households; in Zhongzong's time Princess Taiping reached five thousand households, generally with seven laborers as the cap.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang, a princess's actual fief was capped at three hundred households; under Zhongzong, Princess Taiping held five thousand, generally with seven corvée households per fief household.

sentences.zh: 開元以來，皇妹止千戸，皇女又半之，皆以三丁爲限；

translations.literal: Since the Kaiyuan era, imperial younger sisters were limited to a thousand households and imperial daughters to half that, all with three laborers as the cap;
translations.idiomatic: Since Kaiyuan, the Emperor's younger sisters received at most a thousand households and his daughters half that, each fief limited to three corvée households;

sentences.zh: 駙馬皆除三品員外官，而不任以職事。

translations.literal: sons-in-law were all given third-rank supernumerary offices but were not entrusted with substantive duties.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law were given third-rank supernumerary posts but no substantive office.

sentences.zh: 公主邑入少，至不能具車服，左右或言其太薄，上曰：「百姓租賦，非我所有。

translations.literal: Princesses' fief income was so small they could not even fully equip carriages and robes; attendants sometimes said the allotment was too thin; the Emperor said: "The people's rent and tax are not mine to own.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses' fief income was so meager they could scarcely maintain proper carriages and dress; when attendants said the grants were too thin, the Emperor said: "The people's rent and tax are not my private property.

sentences.zh: 戰士出死力，賞不過束帛；

translations.literal: Warriors who risk death receive rewards of no more than a bundle of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Warriors who risk death receive rewards of no more than a bundle of silk;

sentences.zh: 女子何功，而享多戸邪？

translations.literal: what merit have women that they should enjoy so many households?
translations.idiomatic: what merit have women that they should enjoy so many households?

sentences.zh: 且欲使之知儉嗇耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover I wish them to know thrift and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: I also want them to learn thrift and restraint."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，-{咸}-宜公主將下嫁，始加實封至千戸。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, when Princess Xianyi was about to marry, her actual fief was for the first time increased to a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, as Princess Xianyi prepared to marry, her actual fief was raised for the first time to a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 公主，武惠妃之女也。

translations.literal: The princess was a daughter of Consort Wu Huifei.
translations.idiomatic: She was a daughter of Consort Wu Huifei.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是諸公主皆加至千戸。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the princesses were increased to a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every princess received a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊申，突騎施寇北庭及安西拔換城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the Turgesh raided Beiting and the Anxi garrison at Bahuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the Turgesh raided Beiting and the Anxi garrison at Bahuan.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the renwu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the renwu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙亥，冊故蜀州司戸楊玄琰女爲壽王妃。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yihai, the former daughter of Shu Prefecture Registrar Yang Xuanyan was enfeoffed as consort to Prince Shou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yihai, Yang Xuanyan's daughter, lately a Shu Prefecture registrar's daughter, was made consort to Prince Shou.

sentences.zh: 玄琰，汪之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xuanyan was a great-grandson of Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyan was a great-grandson of Yang Wang.

sentences.zh: 是歳，契丹王過折爲其臣涅禮所殺，-{並}-其諸子，一子刺-{乾}-奔安東得免。

translations.literal: That year the Khitan king Guozhe was killed by his minister Nieli, who killed his sons as well; one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: That year Khitan king Li Guozhe was killed by his minister Nieli together with Guozhe's sons; one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and survived.

sentences.zh: 涅禮上言，過折用刑殘虐，衆情不安，故殺之。

translations.literal: Nieli memorialized that Guozhe's punishments had been cruel and the people's hearts unsettled, and so he had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli reported that Guozhe's punishments were cruel and the people uneasy, which was why he had killed him.

sentences.zh: 上赦其罪，因以涅禮爲-{松}-漠都督，且賜書責之曰：「卿之蕃法多無義-{於}-君長，自昔如此，朕亦知之。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned his crime, made Nieli Military Commissioner of Songmo, and also sent a letter rebuking him: "Your tribal law often shows no righteousness toward its lords; it has been so from old, and I know it too.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned him, appointed Nieli Military Commissioner of Songmo, and sent a rebuking letter: "Your tribal customs often lack loyalty to chiefs—as they always have, and I know it.

sentences.zh: 然過折是卿之王，有惡輒殺之，爲此王者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Yet Guozhe was your king; when there was evil you killed him—is it not hard to be such a king!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guozhe was your king; you killed him for his faults—is such a kingship not precarious!

sentences.zh: 但恐卿今爲王，-{後}-人亦爾。

translations.literal: I only fear that when you are king now, others will act likewise toward you.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that now you are king, others will treat you the same way.

sentences.zh: 常不自保，誰-{願}-作王！

translations.literal: You cannot long keep yourself safe—who would wish to be king!
translations.idiomatic: You cannot long keep yourself safe—who would wish to be king!

sentences.zh: 亦應防慮-{後}-事，豈得取快目前！」

translations.literal: You should also guard against what comes after; how can you take present satisfaction alone!
translations.idiomatic: You should also guard against what comes after; how can you take present satisfaction alone!

sentences.zh: 突厥尋引兵東侵奚、契丹，涅禮與奚王李歸國共撃破之。

translations.literal: The Turks soon led troops east to invade the Xi and Khitan; Nieli and the Xi king Li Guiguo together defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks soon invaded the Xi and Khitan eastward; Nieli and Xi king Li Guiguo jointly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚寅，敕：「天下逃戸，-{聽}-盡今年内自首，有舊産者令還本貫，無者別俟進止；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengyin, an edict: "Fugitive households throughout the realm are permitted to surrender within this year; those with former property are to return to their original registers, those without are to await further orders separately;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengyin, an edict: "Fugitive households empire-wide may surrender within this year; those with former property shall return to their home registers, those without shall await separate orders;

sentences.zh: 逾限不首，當命專使搜求，散配諸軍。」

translations.literal: those who fail to surrender after the deadline will be sought by special envoys and dispersed among the armies."
translations.idiomatic: those who fail to surrender after the deadline will be sought by special envoys and assigned to the armies."

sentences.zh: 北庭都護蓋嘉運撃突騎施，大破之。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Beiting Gai Jiayun attacked the Turgesh and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Beiting Protector-General Gai Jiayun attacked the Turgesh and routed them.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，宴新除縣令-{於}-朝堂，上作《令長新戒》一篇，賜天下縣令。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, the Emperor feasted newly appointed county magistrates in the Hall of Court, composed an essay "New Admonition for Magistrates," and bestowed it on magistrates throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, he feasted newly appointed county magistrates in court, wrote "New Admonition for Magistrates," and gave it to every county magistrate in the empire.

sentences.zh: 庚午，更皇子名：鴻曰瑛，潭曰琮，浚曰璵，洽曰琰，涓曰瑤，滉曰琬，水居曰琚，濰曰璲，沄曰□，澤曰璘，淸曰瑁，回曰玢，沐曰琦，溢曰環，沔曰理，泚曰玼漼曰珪，澄曰珙，潓曰瑱，漎曰璿，滔曰璥。

translations.literal: On gengwu the imperial sons' names were changed: Hong to Ying, Tan to Cong, Jun to Yu, He to Yan, Juan to Yao, Huang to Wan, Shuiju to Ju, Wei to Sui, Yun to [character lost], Ze to Lin, Qing to Mao, Hui to Bin, Mu to Qi, Yi to Huan, Mian to Li, Ci to Ci, Cui to Gui, Cheng to Gong, Hui to Zhen, Long to Xuan, Tao to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the princes were renamed: Li Hong became Ying, Tan became Cong, Jun became Yu, He became Yan, Juan became Yao, Huang became Wan, Shuiju became Ju, Wei became Sui, Yun became [character lost], Ze became Lin, Qing became Mao, Hui became Bin, Mu became Qi, Yi became Huan, Mian became Li, Ci became Ci, Cui became Gui, Cheng became Gong, Hui became Zhen, Long became Xuan, Tao became Jin.

sentences.zh: 舊-{制}-，考功員外郎掌試貢舉人。

translations.literal: By old regulation, the Evaluation Bureau outside-section member oversaw examination of tribute candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, the Evaluation Bureau outside-section member conducted the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 有進士李權，陵侮員外郎李昂，議者以員外郎位卑，不能服衆；

translations.literal: There was a presented scholar named Li Quan who insulted Outside-Section Member Li Ang; deliberators held that the outside-section post was too lowly to command respect from all;
translations.idiomatic: When presented scholar Li Quan insulted Outside-Section Member Li Ang, officials argued the post was too low in rank to command the candidates' respect;

sentences.zh: 三月，壬辰，敕自今委禮部侍郎試貢舉人。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renchen, an edict ordered that from now on the Vice Minister of Rites should conduct the examination of tribute candidates.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renchen, an edict transferred examination of tribute candidates to the Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 張守珪使平盧討撃使、左驍衞將軍安祿山討奚、契丹叛者，祿山恃勇輕進，爲虜所敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui sent Pinglu Strike Commissioner and Left Brave Guard General An Lushan to attack Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, relying on his courage, advanced rashly and was defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui sent Pinglu Strike Commissioner and Left Brave Guard General An Lushan against Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, overconfident, advanced rashly and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，守珪奏請斬之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Shougui memorialized requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Shougui memorialized asking that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 祿山臨刑呼曰：「大夫不欲滅奚、契丹邪！

translations.literal: As Lushan faced execution he cried: "Commissioner, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Lushan cried: "Commissioner, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!

sentences.zh: 奈何殺祿山！」

translations.literal: Why kill Lushan!
translations.idiomatic: Why kill Lushan!

sentences.zh: 守珪亦惜其驍勇，欲活之，乃更執送京師。

translations.literal: Shougui also prized his fierce valor and wished to spare him, and so bound him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui, valuing his fighting skill, wished to spare him and sent him to the capital under guard instead.

sentences.zh: 張九齡批曰：「昔穰苴誅莊賈，孫武斬宮嬪。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling annotated: "In the past Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling wrote in the margin: "Long ago Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.

sentences.zh: 守珪軍令若行，祿山不宜免死。」

translations.literal: If Shougui's military law were enforced, Lushan ought not to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: If Shougui enforced military law, Lushan should not have been spared.

sentences.zh: 上惜其-{才}-，敕令免官，以白衣將領。

translations.literal: The Emperor prized his talent and ordered him pardoned from office, to lead troops as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor prized his talent, pardoned him from office, and let him lead troops in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 九齡固爭曰：「祿山失律喪師，-{於}-法不可不誅。

translations.literal: Jiuling firmly remonstrated: "Lushan violated discipline and lost the army; by law he cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling insisted: "Lushan broke discipline and lost his army; by law he must die.

sentences.zh: 且臣觀其貌有反相，不殺必爲-{後}-患。」

translations.literal: Moreover I observe that his appearance has the look of a rebel; if he is not killed he will surely become a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I see rebel features in his face; if he is not killed he will become a future scourge.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫識石勒，枉害忠良。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le, wrongly harm a loyal man.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu mistaking Shi Le, wrongly destroy a loyal man.

sentences.zh: 竟赦之。

translations.literal: In the end he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 安祿山者，本營州雜胡，初名阿犖山。

translations.literal: An Lushan was originally a mixed Hu of Ying Prefecture; his original name was Aluoshan.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan was originally a mixed Hu from Ying Prefecture; his birth name was Aluoshan.

sentences.zh: 其母，巫也；

translations.literal: His mother was a shaman;
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a shaman;

sentences.zh: 父死，母攜之再-{適}-突厥安延偃。

translations.literal: after his father died his mother carried him and remarried the Turk An Yanyan.
translations.idiomatic: after his father died his mother remarried the Turk An Yanyan and took the boy with her.

sentences.zh: 會其部落破散，與延偃兄子思順倶逃來，故冒姓安氏，名祿山。

translations.literal: When their tribe was broken and scattered, he fled together with Yanyan's nephew An Sishun; therefore he took the surname An and the name Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: When their tribe broke up, he fled with Yanyan's nephew An Sishun, took the surname An, and was called Lushan.

sentences.zh: 又有史窣-{干}-者，與祿山同裡閉，先-{後}-一日生。

translations.literal: There was also one Shi Suogan of the same neighborhood, born one day before or after him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Suogan, from the same neighborhood, was born a day apart from him.

sentences.zh: 及長，相親愛，皆爲互市牙郎，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: When grown they were close friends; both became brokers in the border markets and were known for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: As youths they were close; both became frontier trade brokers and won fame for courage.

sentences.zh: 張守珪以祿山爲捉生將，祿山毎與數騎出，輒擒契丹數十人而返。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui made Lushan a captive-taking officer; each time Lushan went out with several horsemen he would seize several dozen Khitan and return.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui made Lushan a captive-taking officer; riding out with a few men he would capture dozens of Khitan at a time.

sentences.zh: 狡黠，善揣人情，守珪愛之，養以爲子。

translations.literal: Cunning and skilled at reading men's feelings, Shougui loved him and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty and adept at reading men, Shougui favored him and adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-嘗負官債亡入奚中，爲奚-{游}-弈所得，欲殺之；

translations.literal: Suogan once bore official debt, fled into the Xi, and was seized by Xi game-hunters who wished to kill him;
translations.idiomatic: Suogan once fled into the Xi to escape official debt; Xi hunters seized him and meant to kill him;

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-紿曰：「我，唐之和親使也。

translations.literal: Suogan deceived them, saying: "I am an envoy of Tang's marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Suogan lied: "I am an envoy of Tang's marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 汝殺我，禍且及汝國。」

translations.literal: If you kill me, disaster will reach your state.
translations.idiomatic: If you kill me, disaster will reach your state.

sentences.zh: -{游}-弈信之，送詣牙帳。

translations.literal: The game-hunters believed him and sent him to the royal tent.
translations.idiomatic: The hunters believed him and sent him to the royal tent.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-見奚王，長揖不拜，奚王雖怒，而畏唐，不敢殺，以客禮館之，使百人隨窣-{干}-入朝。

translations.literal: Suogan saw the Xi king, made a long bow without kneeling; though the Xi king was angry, he feared Tang and did not dare kill him, but lodged him with guest rites and sent a hundred men to follow Suogan to court.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Xi king he bowed without kneeling; though the king was furious, he feared Tang and entertained him as a guest, sending a hundred men to escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-謂奚王曰：「王所遣人雖多，觀其-{才}-皆不足以見天子。

translations.literal: Suogan told the Xi king: "Though you send many men, I see that none has talent enough to meet the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Suogan told the Xi king: "Your envoys are many, but none seem fit to meet the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 聞王有良將瑣髙者，何不使之入朝！」

translations.literal: I hear you have a good general named Suogao—why not send him to court!
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have a capable general, Suogao—why not send him!

sentences.zh: 奚王即命瑣髙與牙下三百人隨窣-{干}-入朝。

translations.literal: The Xi king at once ordered Suogao and three hundred men of the yamen to follow Suogan to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi king then sent Suogao with three hundred yamen troops to accompany Suogan to court.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-將至平盧，先使人謂軍使裴休子曰：「奚使瑣髙與精鋭倶來，聲-{雲}-入朝，實欲襲軍城，宜謹爲之備，先事圖之。」

translations.literal: When Suogan was about to reach Pinglu he first sent word to Military Commissioner Pei Xiuzi: "The Xi envoy Suogao is coming with picked troops; he proclaims that he is entering court but in truth intends to raid the garrison—you should prepare carefully and strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Near Pinglu he warned Military Commissioner Pei Xiuzi: "Xi envoy Suogao comes with elite troops claiming to pay court, but intends to raid the garrison—prepare and strike first.

sentences.zh: 休子乃具軍容出迎，至館，悉坑殺其從兵，執瑣髙送幽州。

translations.literal: Xiuzi then arrayed troops to welcome them; when they reached the lodge he buried all the followers in pits and sent Suogao bound to You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzi marched out to receive them, then at the lodge slaughtered the escort and sent Suogao bound to You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張守珪以窣-{干}-爲有功，奏爲果毅，累遷將軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui memorialized that Suogan had merit and had him appointed Fruit-Stalwart, with repeated promotion to general.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui memorialized Suogan's merit; he was made Fruit-Stalwart and rose to general.

sentences.zh: -{後}-入奏事，上與語，悅之，賜名思明。

translations.literal: Later when he entered to memorialize, the Emperor conversed with him, was pleased, and bestowed the name Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Later, appearing at court, he pleased the Emperor, who bestowed the name Siming.

sentences.zh: 故連州司馬武攸望之子温愼，坐交通權貴，杖死。

translations.literal: Former Lian Prefecture Registrar Wen Shen, son of Wu Youwang, was beaten to death for trafficking with powerful men.
translations.idiomatic: Former Lian Prefecture Registrar Wen Shen, son of Wu Youwang, was flogged to death for dealings with powerful men.

sentences.zh: 乙-{丑}-，朔方、河東節度使信安王禕貶衢州刺史，廣武王承宏貶房州別駕，涇州刺史薛自勸貶澧州別駕；

translations.literal: On yichou, Shuo-fang and Hedong Military Commissioner Prince Xin'an Li Yi was demoted to Prefect of Qu Prefecture, Prince Guangwu Li Chenghong to Vice-Prefect of Fang Prefecture, and Jing Prefecture Inspector Xue Ziqin to Vice-Prefect of Li Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Prince Xin'an Li Yi was demoted from Shuo-fang and Hedong commissioner to Qu Prefecture, Prince Guangwu Li Chenghong to Fang Vice-Prefect, and Jing Inspector Xue Ziqin to Li Vice-Prefect;

sentences.zh: 皆坐與温愼交-{遊}-故也。

translations.literal: all for associating with Wen Shen.
translations.idiomatic: all for associating with Wen Shen.

sentences.zh: 承宏，守禮之子也。

translations.literal: Chenghong was a son of Shouli.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghong was a son of Li Shouli.

sentences.zh: 辛未，蒲州刺史王琚貶通州刺史；

translations.literal: On xinwei, Pu Prefecture Inspector Wang Ju was demoted to Prefect of Tong Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Pu Prefecture Inspector Wang Ju was demoted to Tong Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 坐禕交書也。

translations.literal: for exchanging letters with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: for exchanging letters with Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 五月，醴泉妖人劉-{志}-誠作亂，驅掠路人，將趣-{咸}-陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the sorcerer Liu Zhicheng of Liquan raised rebellion, driving and plundering wayfarers, intending to march on Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Liquan sorcerer Liu Zhicheng rebelled, seizing travelers and heading for Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 邨民走告縣官，焚橋斷路以拒之，其衆遂潰。

translations.literal: Villagers ran to inform the county office; they burned bridges and blocked roads to resist, and the band dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers alerted the county, burned bridges, and blocked the roads; the mob broke up.

sentences.zh: 數日，悉擒斬之。

translations.literal: Within several days all were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Within days all were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 六月，初分月給百官俸錢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, for the first time officials' salary cash was issued monthly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, officials began receiving salary cash in monthly installments.

sentences.zh: 初，上因藉田赦，命有司議增宗廟籩豆之-{薦}-及服紀未通者。

translations.literal: Earlier, because of the amnesty at the plowing ceremony, the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to deliberate increasing the ancestral temple's platters and beans for offerings and matters where mourning garb had not yet been harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, using the plowing-ceremony amnesty, he ordered discussion of increasing ancestral offerings and unresolved mourning regulations.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋縚奏請宗廟毎坐籩豆十二。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tao memorialized that each seat in the ancestral temple should have twelve platters and beans.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Wei Tao asked that each ancestral seat have twelve platters and beans.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎張均、職方郎中韋述議曰：「聖人知孝人之情深而物類之無限，故爲之節-{制}-。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Bureau Director Wei Shu argued: "The sage knows that a filial son's feeling runs deep while the kinds of things are limitless, and therefore sets regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Bureau Director Wei Shu argued: "The sage knows a filial child's feelings run deep while offerings are limitless, and therefore sets bounds.

sentences.zh: 人之嗜好本無憑準，宴私之饌與時遷移，故聖人一切同歸-{於}-古。

translations.literal: Men's appetites originally have no fixed standard; private feast foods shift with the times, and so the sage brings all alike back to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Human tastes have no fixed measure; private delicacies change with fashion, so the sage returns all to ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 屈到嗜芰，屈建不以-{薦}-，以爲不以私慾-{干}-國之典。

translations.literal: Qu Dao loved water caltrop, but Qu Jian did not offer it at sacrifice, holding that private desire must not disturb the state's ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Dao loved water caltrop, but Qu Jian would not offer it, holding private appetite must not disturb state ritual.

sentences.zh: 今欲取甘旨肥濃，皆充祭用，苟逾舊-{制}-，其何限焉！

translations.literal: Now if sweet and rich delicacies are all used in sacrifice, and the old system is exceeded, what limit would there be!
translations.idiomatic: If every rich delicacy one enjoys in life were placed on the altar, what limit could there be!

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。』

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Millet and sacrificial millet are not fragrant; bright virtue alone is fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Grain offerings are not fragrant; bright virtue alone is fragrant.

sentences.zh: 若以今之珍饌，平生所習，求神無方，何必泥古，則簠簋可去而盤盂杯案當在-{御}-矣，韶濩可息而箜篌箏笛當在奏矣。

translations.literal: If one uses present delicacies, things one is used to in life, and seeks the spirits without method, why cling to antiquity—then the grain vessels could be removed and platters, bowls, cups, and stands should be at hand; the Shao and Huo dances could cease and konghou, zithers, flutes, and pipes should be performing.
translations.idiomatic: If present delicacies and lifelong tastes are offered because any method will reach the gods, why cling to antiquity—then the grain vessels could go and platters and cups take their place; court music could cease and everyday instruments play instead.

sentences.zh: 既非正物，-{後}-嗣何觀！

translations.literal: Since these are not correct ritual objects, what will later generations see!
translations.idiomatic: If these are not proper ritual objects, what will posterity see!

sentences.zh: 夫神，以精明臨人者也，不求-{豐}-大；

translations.literal: The spirits, by their clarity and intelligence, oversee men and do not seek abundance;
translations.idiomatic: Spirits oversee men through luminous intelligence and do not seek abundance;

sentences.zh: 苟失-{於}-禮，雖多何爲！

translations.literal: if ritual is lost, what good are many offerings!
translations.idiomatic: if ritual fails, what good are many offerings!

sentences.zh: 豈可廢棄禮經以從流俗！

translations.literal: How can one abandon the ritual classics to follow passing custom!
translations.idiomatic: How can one abandon the classics to follow passing fashion!

sentences.zh: 且君子愛人以禮，不求苟合；

translations.literal: Moreover the gentleman cherishes others with ritual and does not seek careless agreement;
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman treats others by ritual, not by careless indulgence;

sentences.zh: 況在宗廟，敢忘舊章？」

translations.literal: how much more in the ancestral temple—dare one forget the old statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: how much less in the ancestral temple may one forget the old statutes?"

sentences.zh: 太子賓客崔沔議曰：「祭祀之興，肇-{於}-太古。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Guest Cui Hao argued: "The rise of sacrifice began in utmost antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Guest Cui Hao argued: "Sacrifice arose in deepest antiquity.

sentences.zh: 茹毛飲血，則有毛血之-{薦}-；

translations.literal: When men ate raw flesh and drank blood, there were offerings of fur and blood;
translations.idiomatic: When men ate raw flesh and drank blood, they offered fur and blood;

sentences.zh: 未有-{麴}-薛，則有玄酒之奠。

translations.literal: before there were yeast and leavened bread, there was the dark-wine offering.
translations.idiomatic: before yeast and leavened bread existed, they offered dark wine.

sentences.zh: 施及-{後}-王，禮物漸備；

translations.literal: Extending to later kings, ritual objects gradually became complete;
translations.idiomatic: Under later kings ritual objects grew complete;

sentences.zh: 然以神道致敬，不敢廢也。

translations.literal: yet in reverencing the spirit way one did not dare abolish the earlier forms.
translations.idiomatic: yet reverence for the spirits kept the older forms alive.

sentences.zh: 籩豆簠簋樽罍之實，皆周人之時饌也，其用通-{於}-宴饗賓客，而周公-{制}-禮，與毛血玄酒同-{薦}-鬼神。

translations.literal: The contents of platters, beans, grain vessels, and wine vessels were all Zhou people's contemporary foods; their use extended to feasts and guests, yet the Duke of Zhou established ritual and offered them to the spirits together with fur and blood and dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: Platters, beans, vessels, and wine were Zhou daily fare, used also at banquets; yet the Duke of Zhou placed them before the spirits beside fur, blood, and dark wine.

sentences.zh: 國家由禮立訓，因時-{制}--{范}-，淸廟時饗，禮饌必陳，用周-{制}-也。

translations.literal: The state stands on ritual to establish instruction and fashions norms according to the times; in the Clear Temple seasonal feasting ritual foods must be set out—this follows Zhou usage.
translations.idiomatic: The state teaches through ritual and adapts norms to the age; Clear Temple seasonal feasts require those foods—following Zhou.

sentences.zh: 園寢上食，時膳具設，遵漢法也。

translations.literal: At the park tombs for the upper offering, seasonal delicacies are fully provided—following Han law.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial park tombs, seasonal dishes are fully set out—following Han practice.

sentences.zh: 職貢來祭，致遠物也。

translations.literal: When tribute missions come to sacrifice, distant products are presented.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute missions come to sacrifice, they present products from afar.

sentences.zh: 有新必-{薦}-，順時令也。

translations.literal: When there is something new, it must be offered—this follows the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever is new must be offered, in accord with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 苑囿之内，躬稼所收，搜狩之時，親-{發}-所中，莫不-{薦}-而-{後}-食，盡誠敬也。

translations.literal: Within the parklands, what was personally reaped in the fields; at times of the hunt, what was personally shot—none was eaten before offering; this is utmost sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In the parks, grain he reaped himself and game he took himself were all offered before he ate—a mark of utter sincerity.

sentences.zh: 若此至矣，-{復}-何加焉！

translations.literal: If it has reached this point, what further increase is there!
translations.idiomatic: When devotion already reaches this pitch, what could be added!

sentences.zh: 但當申敕有司，無或簡怠，則鮮美肥濃，盡在是矣，不必加籩豆之數也。」

translations.literal: One need only instruct the responsible offices sternly that none be negligent or slack, and fresh, fine, rich flavors will all be here—there is no need to increase the number of platters and beans."
translations.idiomatic: Simply command the responsible offices not to slacken, and every delicacy will already be present—no need to add platters and beans."

sentences.zh: 上固欲量加品味。

translations.literal: The Emperor had firmly intended to add to the varieties of flavor by degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still meant to increase the menu by degrees.

sentences.zh: 縚又奏毎室加籩豆各六，四時各實以新果珍羞；

translations.literal: Tao again memorialized that each shrine should add six platters and beans each, each season filled with fresh fruits and rare delicacies;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tao memorialized further that each shrine add six platters and beans apiece, stocked each season with fresh fruit and fine food;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 縚又奏：「《喪服》『舅，緦麻三月，從母，外祖父母皆小功五月。』

translations.literal: Tao again memorialized: "The 'Mourning Garb' says: 'For maternal uncle, sima hemp three months; for mother's sister, maternal grandparents, all xiao mourning five months.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tao memorialized again: "The Mourning Garb states: 'For maternal uncle, three months in sima hemp; for mother's sister and maternal grandparents, five months in xiao mourning.

sentences.zh: 外祖至尊，同-{於}-從母之服；

translations.literal: Maternal grandparents are supremely honored, yet wear the same mourning as a mother's sister;
translations.idiomatic: Yet maternal grandparents, though greatly honored, wear the same grade as a mother's sister;

sentences.zh: 姨、舅一等，服則輕重有殊。

translations.literal: maternal aunts and maternal uncles are one kin category, yet the mourning grades differ in weight and lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal aunts and uncles are one kin level, yet the mourning differs in weight.

sentences.zh: 堂姨、舅親即未疎，恩絶不相爲服，舅母來承外族，不如同爨之禮。

translations.literal: Paternal-side maternal aunts and uncles, though not distant in kin, have affection severed and do not mourn for one another; an uncle's wife comes as an in-law from the maternal line and is less close than sharing one hearth.
translations.idiomatic: Cousins on the father's side are kin yet need not mourn one another; an uncle's wife inherits the maternal connection but lacks the bond of one household.

sentences.zh: 竊以古意猶有所未暢者也，請加外祖父母爲大功九月，姨、舅皆小功五月，堂舅、堂姨、舅母-{並}-加至袒免。」

translations.literal: I privately deem that ancient intent is not yet fully carried through; I ask that maternal grandparents be raised to da mourning nine months, maternal aunts and uncles all to xiao mourning five months, and paternal-side maternal uncles, aunts, and uncles' wives all raised to bare-shoulder mourning."
translations.idiomatic: I believe the ancients' intent is not yet fully realized: raise maternal grandparents to nine months of da mourning, aunts and maternal uncles to five months of xiao mourning, and paternal-side maternal kin and uncles' wives to bare-shoulder mourning."

sentences.zh: 崔沔議曰：「正家之道，不可以貳；

translations.literal: Cui Hao argued: "The Way of rectifying the family cannot be duplicated;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao argued: "The way to order a household admits no duplication;

sentences.zh: 總一定義，理歸本宗。

translations.literal: gathering all under one fixed principle, reason returns to the main lineage.
translations.idiomatic: One fixed principle governs all, and reason belongs to the main line.

sentences.zh: 是以内有齊、斬，外皆緦麻，尊名所加，不過一等，此先王不易之道也。

translations.literal: Thus within there are qi and zhan; without all are sima hemp; the honor of one's title adds no more than one grade—this is the unchanging Way of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Within, mourning runs to qi and zhan; without, to sima hemp; titles add at most one grade—the unchanging Way of former kings.

sentences.zh: -{願}-守八年明旨，一依古禮，以爲萬代成法。」

translations.literal: I wish to uphold the clarified decree of the eighth year and follow ancient ritual entirely, making it the enduring law for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we uphold the eighth-year decree, follow ancient ritual in full, and make it law for all generations."

sentences.zh: 韋述議曰：「《喪服傳》曰：『禽獸知母而不知父。

translations.literal: Wei Shu argued: "The 'Commentary on Mourning Garb' says: 'Beasts know their mothers but not their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu argued: "The Mourning Garb Commentary says: 'Beasts know mother but not father.

sentences.zh: 野人曰，父母何等焉！

translations.literal: The uncultivated man says, how can father and mother be equal!
translations.idiomatic: Rustic men ask how father and mother could be equal!

sentences.zh: 都邑之士則知尊檷矣；

translations.literal: Men of the capital know how to honor their deceased father;
translations.idiomatic: City dwellers learn to honor the deceased father;

sentences.zh: 大夫及學士則知尊祖矣。』

translations.literal: grandees and scholar-officials know how to honor their ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees and scholars learn to honor ancestors.

sentences.zh: 聖人究天道而厚-{於}-祖檷，-{系}-族姓而親其子孫，母黨比-{於}-本族，不可同貫，明矣。

translations.literal: The sage scrutinizes Heaven's Way yet gives weight to ancestors and the deceased father, binds clan names and cherishes descendants, and maternal kin, compared with the main lineage, clearly cannot be treated alike.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way teaches reverence for ancestors and fathers, bonds of surname and blood tie descendants together—maternal kin, unlike the main line, clearly cannot share the same grade.

sentences.zh: 今若外祖及舅加服一等，堂舅及姨列-{於}-服紀，則中外之-{制}-，相去-{幾}-何！

translations.literal: If now maternal grandparents and uncles are raised one grade of mourning, and paternal-side maternal uncles and aunts are placed in the mourning registers, how far apart will inner and outer regulations be!
translations.idiomatic: Raise grandparents and maternal uncles one grade and place paternal-side aunts and uncles on the mourning rolls, and how thin becomes the line between inner and outer kin!

sentences.zh: 廢禮徇情，所務者末。

translations.literal: To abandon ritual and indulge feeling is to pursue what is secondary.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon ritual for feeling is to chase what is least important.

sentences.zh: 古之-{製}-作者，知人情之易搖，恐失禮之將漸，別其同異，輕重相懸，欲使-{後}-來之人永不相雜。

translations.literal: The ancients who fashioned ritual knew how easily human feelings sway and feared the gradual loss of ritual; they distinguished sameness from difference, hung heavy and light far apart, wishing that later generations would never mix them.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual's makers knew how feelings shift and feared gradual decay; they split kin categories and widened the distance between grades so later ages would never blur them.

sentences.zh: 微旨斯在，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: The subtle intent lies here—how could it be mere empty form!
translations.idiomatic: That was the subtle design—not empty ceremony!

sentences.zh: 苟可加也，亦可減也；

translations.literal: If one may add, one may also subtract;
translations.idiomatic: What can be increased can also be cut;

sentences.zh: 往聖可得而非，則《禮經》可得而隳矣。

translations.literal: if former sages may be criticized, then the Classic of Ritual may be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If past sages may be questioned, the Ritual Classic itself may be torn down.

sentences.zh: 先王之-{制}-，謂之彝倫，奉以周旋，猶恐失墜；

translations.literal: Former kings' institutions are called the constant norms; even in observing them daily one still fears losing them;
translations.idiomatic: Former kings called their institutions the eternal norms; even in daily observance one fears their loss;

sentences.zh: 一紊其敘，庸可止乎！

translations.literal: once their order is disrupted, can it ever be stopped!
translations.idiomatic: Once order is tangled, can collapse be halted!

sentences.zh: 請依《儀禮》喪服爲定。」

translations.literal: I ask that mourning garb be fixed according to the Ceremonial Rituals."
translations.idiomatic: Fix mourning grades by the Ceremonial Rituals."

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎楊仲昌議曰：「鄭文貞公魏-{-{徴}-}-始加舅服至小功五月。

translations.literal: Deputy Director of Rites Yang Zhongchang argued: "Duke Wen Zhen, Wei Zheng, first raised mourning for maternal uncles to xiao mourning five months.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Director of Rites Yang Zhongchang argued: "Duke Wen Zhen Wei Zheng first raised mourning for maternal uncles to five months of xiao mourning.

sentences.zh: 雖文貞賢也，而周、孔聖也，以賢改聖，-{後}-學何從！

translations.literal: Though Wen Zhen was worthy, Zhou and Confucius were sages; to have the worthy alter the sages—what are later students to follow!
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhen was worthy, but Zhou and Confucius were sages—when the worthy alter the sages, what can later students follow?

sentences.zh: 竊恐内外乖序，親疎奪倫，情之所沿，何所不至！

translations.literal: I privately fear inner and outer will fall out of order, closeness and distance will usurp their ranks, and where feeling leads, what limit will there be!
translations.idiomatic: I fear inner and outer kin will lose order, closeness and distance will overturn hierarchy—and where feeling leads, what will not follow!

sentences.zh: 昔子路有姊之喪而不除，孔子曰：『先王-{制}-禮，行道之人，皆不忍也。』

translations.literal: Once Zilu had mourning for his elder sister and did not doff the garb; Confucius said: 'Former kings made ritual, yet even travelers on the road could not bear to follow it.'
translations.idiomatic: Once Zilu wore mourning for his elder sister and refused to doff it; Confucius said: 'Former kings made ritual that even wayfarers found hard to bear.'

sentences.zh: 子路除之。

translations.literal: Zilu removed the mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Zilu removed the garb.

sentences.zh: 此則聖人援事抑情之明例也。

translations.literal: This is the sage's clear example of citing an occasion to restrain feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Here is the sage's clear lesson: use the occasion to restrain feeling.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：『無輕議禮。』

translations.literal: The Record says: 'Do not lightly debate ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: 'Do not lightly debate ritual.'

sentences.zh: 明其蟠-{於}-天地，-{並}-彼日月，賢者由之，安敢損益也！」

translations.literal: It makes clear that ritual coils through Heaven and Earth, stands with sun and moon; worthy men follow it—how dare one add or subtract!"
translations.idiomatic: Ritual coils through Heaven and Earth and stands with sun and moon; worthy men follow it—who dares alter it!"

sentences.zh: 敕：「姨舅既服小功，舅母不得全降，宜服緦麻，堂姨舅宜服袒免。」

translations.literal: An edict: "Since maternal aunts and uncles already wear xiao mourning, an uncle's wife cannot be fully reduced; she should wear sima hemp; paternal-side maternal aunts and uncles should wear bare-shoulder mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "Maternal aunts and uncles having xiao mourning, an uncle's wife should not be fully reduced but wear sima hemp; paternal-side maternal kin should wear bare-shoulder mourning."

sentences.zh: 均，説之子也。

translations.literal: Jun was the son of Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was a son of Zhang Shuo.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬子，千秋節，群臣皆獻寶鏡。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on renzi, the Thousand Autumns Festival, all ministers presented precious mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on renzi—the Thousand Autumns Festival—ministers presented precious mirrors.

sentences.zh: 張九齡以爲以鏡自照見形容，以人自照見吉凶，乃述前世興廢之源，爲書五巻，謂之《千秋金鏡録》，上之；

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling held that a mirror shows one's form when one looks at oneself, and men show fortune and misfortune when one looks at men; he therefore traced the sources of rise and fall in former ages and wrote five scrolls called Records of the Thousand Autumns Golden Mirror, presenting it to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling reasoned that mirrors reveal one's face and worthy men reveal fortune and ruin; tracing rise and fall in past ages he wrote five scrolls, Records of the Thousand Autumns Golden Mirror, and presented them.

sentences.zh: 上賜書褒美。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a letter in praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied with a letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，突騎施遣其大臣胡祿達-{干}-來請降，許之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Turgesh sent their minister Hulu Daghan to request surrender; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the Turgesh sent Minister Hulu Daghan to surrender; the Emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史大夫李-{適}-之，承-{乾}-之孫也，以-{才}--{幹}-得幸-{於}-上，數爲承-{乾}-論辨；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi, grandson of Chengqian, through talent and ability won the Emperor's favor and repeatedly argued on Chengqian's behalf;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi, grandson of Li Chengqian, won favor through talent and repeatedly defended Chengqian's reputation.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，追贈承-{乾}-恆山愍王。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Chengqian was posthumously created Prince Min of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Chengqian was posthumously ennobled Prince Min of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，汴哀王璥薨。

translations.literal: On yihai, Prince Ai of Bian, Li Jin, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Prince Ai of Bian, Li Jin, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊申，車駕-{發}-東都。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the imperial carriage set out from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the Emperor left the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，敕以來年二月二日行幸西京，會宮中有怪，明日，上召宰相，即議西還。

translations.literal: Previously an edict had set the second day of the second month of the coming year for traveling to the Western Capital; then strange happenings occurred in the palace, and the next day the Emperor summoned the chief ministers and immediately deliberated returning west.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had scheduled travel to Chang'an for the second day of the second month; when omens appeared in the palace, the Emperor summoned his chancellors the next day and moved to return west at once.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿、張九齡曰：「今農收未畢，請俟仲冬。」

translations.literal: Pei Yaoji and Zhang Jiuling said: "The harvest is not yet complete; we ask to wait until mid-winter."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoji and Zhang Jiuling said: "Harvest is not finished—please wait until mid-winter."

sentences.zh: 李林甫潛知上指，二相退，林甫獨留，言-{於}-上曰：「長安、洛陽，陛下東西宮耳，往來行幸，何更擇時！

translations.literal: Li Linfu secretly knew the Emperor's intent; when the two chancellors withdrew, Linfu alone remained and said to the Emperor: "Chang'an and Luoyang are Your Majesty's eastern and western palaces; coming and going is imperial travel—why choose the season!
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had sensed the Emperor's mind; when the others withdrew he stayed behind and said: "Chang'an and Luoyang are your two palaces—why fuss over timing for a move between them!

sentences.zh: 借使妨-{於}-農收，但應蠲所過租稅而已。

translations.literal: Even if it impedes the harvest, one need only remit rent and tax along the route.
translations.idiomatic: Even if harvest suffers, remit taxes along the route—that suffices.

sentences.zh: 臣請宣示百司，即日西行。」

translations.literal: I ask to announce this to the hundred offices and travel west this very day."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you notify every office and set out west today."

sentences.zh: 上悅，從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased, the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 過陝州，以刺史盧奐有善政，題贊-{於}-其-{聽}-事而去。

translations.literal: Passing through Shaanzhou, because Prefect Lu Huan had good governance, he inscribed praise in the hall of audience and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Shaanzhou, he inscribed praise in Prefect Lu Huan's hall of audience for his good rule and moved on.

sentences.zh: 奐，懷愼之子也。

translations.literal: Huan was the son of Huaishen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huan was a son of Lu Huaishen.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至西京。

translations.literal: On dingmao, he reached the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使牛仙客，前在河西，能節用度，勤職業，倉庫充實，器械精利；

translations.literal: Shuofang Military Commissioner Niu Xianke, while previously in Hexi, could economize expenses, diligently perform his duties, fill the granaries, and keep weapons sharp;
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang commander Niu Xianke, formerly in Hexi, had economized diligently, filled granaries, and kept arms in fine order;

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，欲加尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and praised this, wishing to promote him to Director of a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the Emperor wished to make him a Director of one of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 張九齡曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling objected: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 尚書，古之納言，唐興以來，惟舊相及揚歴中外有德望者乃爲之。

translations.literal: Director of a ministry was the ancient office of Grand Counselor; since the Tang arose, only former chancellors and men who had risen through central and provincial posts with virtue and standing had held it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry directorship was antiquity's Grand Counselor; since Tang's founding only former chancellors and men of proven virtue and standing across court and provinces had held it.

sentences.zh: 仙客本河湟使典，今驟居淸要，恐羞朝廷。」
