translations.literal: Xianke was originally a clerk in the Hexi command; to place him suddenly in a pure, vital post would, I fear, bring shame on the court."
translations.idiomatic: Xianke was a frontier clerk; to thrust him suddenly into a premier post would shame the court."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然則但加實封可乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then would adding to his actual fief alone suffice?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "Then might an increase to his fief alone suffice?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不可。

translations.literal: He replied: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling answered: "No.

sentences.zh: 封爵所以勸有功也。

translations.literal: Enfeoffment and nobility exist to encourage meritorious achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and fiefs reward real achievement.

sentences.zh: 邊將實倉庫，修器械，乃常務耳，不足爲功。

translations.literal: For a frontier general to fill granaries and repair weapons is ordinary duty and not enough to count as merit.
translations.idiomatic: Filling stores and sharpening arms is ordinary duty for a frontier commander—not merit enough for enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 陛下賞其勤，賜之金帛可也；

translations.literal: Your Majesty may reward his diligence with gold and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Reward his diligence with gold and silk;

sentences.zh: 裂土封之，恐非其宜。」

translations.literal: but to carve out land and enfeoff him would, I fear, be inappropriate."
translations.idiomatic: but carving out fief land would be inappropriate."

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 李林甫言-{於}-上曰：「仙客，宰相-{才}-也，何有-{於}-尚書！

translations.literal: Li Linfu said to the Emperor: "Xianke has the talent of a chancellor—what is a ministry directorship to him!
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu told the Emperor: "Xianke has chancellor's talent—a ministry directorship is beneath him!

sentences.zh: 九齡書生，不達大體。」

translations.literal: Jiuling is a bookish man who does not grasp the larger design."
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling is a pedant who misses the larger picture."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 明日，-{復}-以仙客實封爲言，九齡固執如初。

translations.literal: The next day, when the topic of Xianke's actual fief was raised again, Jiuling stood firm as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Xianke's fief came up again, Jiuling held firm as before.

sentences.zh: 上怒，變色曰：「事皆由卿邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry, his face changing, and said: "Must every matter go through you?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flushed with anger: "Must everything go your way?"

sentences.zh: 九齡頓首謝曰：「陛下不知臣愚，使待罪宰相，事有未允，臣不敢不盡言。」

translations.literal: Jiuling bowed with his head to the ground and said: "Your Majesty does not know my stupidity; having charged me as chancellor bearing guilt, when matters are unsuitable I dare not fail to speak fully."
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling kowtowed: "Your Majesty, not knowing my dullness, made me chancellor; when something seems wrong I dare not hold back."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿嫌仙客寒微，如卿有何閥閲！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You despise Xianke as low-born—what noble lineage do you have!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor snapped: "You think Xianke too humble—what noble lineage have you!"

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「臣嶺海孤賤，不如仙客生-{於}-中華；

translations.literal: Jiuling said: "I am a solitary outcast of the Lingnan seas, lower-born than Xianke, who was born in central China;
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling replied: "I am a lowly southerner, less well born than Xianke of the heartland;

sentences.zh: 然臣出入-{台}-閣，典司誥命有年矣。

translations.literal: yet I have moved in and out of the secretariat and for years presided over imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: yet I have served in the secretariat and drafted imperial edicts for years.

sentences.zh: 仙客邊隅小吏，目不知書，若大任之，恐不愜衆望。」

translations.literal: Xianke is a petty clerk from the borderlands who cannot read; if given a great appointment, I fear public expectation will not be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Xianke is an illiterate frontier clerk; a great appointment would, I fear, disappoint public expectation.

sentences.zh: 林甫退而言曰：「苟有-{才}-識，何必辭學！

translations.literal: When Linfu withdrew he said: "If one has talent and insight, why require literary learning!
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Li Linfu remarked: "If a man has talent, why demand book learning!

sentences.zh: 天子用人，有何不可！」

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven employs men, what may he not do!"
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven may appoint whom he chooses!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊戌，賜仙客爵隴西縣公，食實封三百戸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuxu, Xianke was granted the title Duke of Longxi County with an actual fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuxu, Niu Xianke was ennobled Duke of Longxi with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 初，上欲以李林甫爲相，問-{於}-中書令張九齡，九齡對曰：「宰相-{系}-國安危，陛下相林甫，臣恐異日爲廟社之憂。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor wished to make Li Linfu chancellor, he asked Secretariat Director Zhang Jiuling; Jiuling replied: "The chancellor is tied to the state's safety and peril; if Your Majesty makes Linfu chancellor, I fear one day he will be a concern for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first considered Li Linfu for chancellor, he asked Zhang Jiuling, who said: "The chancellor holds the realm's fate; appoint Linfu and I fear future peril for the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 時九齡方以文學爲上所重，林甫雖恨，猶-{曲}-意事之。

translations.literal: At the time Jiuling was still valued by the Emperor for his literary attainment; though Linfu resented him, he still attended to him with forced deference.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling still enjoyed imperial favor for his literary gifts; though Linfu hated him, he feigned deference.

sentences.zh: 侍中裴耀卿與九齡善，林甫-{並}-疾之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Pei Yaoji was on good terms with Jiuling, and Linfu hated them both.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Pei Yaoji, Jiuling's ally, Linfu hated equally.

sentences.zh: 是時，上在位歳久，漸肆奢欲，怠-{於}-政事。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor had been on the throne many years and gradually indulged luxurious desires, growing slack in governance.
translations.idiomatic: By now the Emperor had reigned long, indulging luxury and neglecting governance.

sentences.zh: 而九齡遇事無細大皆力爭；

translations.literal: Jiuling, on every matter great or small, strove with all his strength;
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling contested every matter, large or small;

sentences.zh: 林甫巧伺上意，日思所以中傷之。

translations.literal: while Linfu craftily watched the Emperor's intent and daily sought means to wound him.
translations.idiomatic: while Linfu watched the Emperor's mood and daily schemed to undermine him.

sentences.zh: 上之爲臨淄王也，趙麗妃、皇甫德儀、劉-{才}-人皆有寵，麗妃生太子瑛，德儀生鄂王瑤，-{才}-人生光王琚。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had been Prince of Linzi, Consort Zhao Lifi, Consort Huangfu Deyi, and Lady Liu the Talented were all favored; Lifi bore Crown Prince Ying, Deyi bore Prince E Yao, and the Talented Lady bore Prince Guang Ju.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince of Linzi he had favored Consort Zhao Lifi, Consort Huangfu Deyi, and Lady Liu; Lifi bore Crown Prince Ying, Deyi bore Prince E Yao, and Lady Liu bore Prince Guang Ju.

sentences.zh: 及即位，幸武惠妃，麗妃等愛皆馳；

translations.literal: After his accession he favored Consort Wu Huifei, and affection for Lifi and the others slackened;
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement he favored Consort Wu Huifei, and the others waned in favor;

sentences.zh: 惠妃生壽王瑁，寵冠諸子。

translations.literal: Huifei bore Prince Shou Mao, whose favor surpassed all other sons.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei bore Prince Shou Li Mao, favored above all other sons.

sentences.zh: 太子與瑤、琚會-{於}-内第，各以母失職有怨望語。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince met with Yao and Ju in the inner quarters, each speaking resentfully of his mother's loss of favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince met Yao and Ju privately, each venting resentment over his mother's fall from favor.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉楊洄尚-{咸}-宜公主，常伺三子過失以告惠妃。

translations.literal: Commandant of Cavaliers Yang Hui, who had married Princess Xianyi, constantly watched the three sons' faults and reported them to Huifei.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Cavaliers Yang Hui, married to Princess Xianyi, constantly watched the three princes' missteps and reported them to Consort Wu Huifei.

sentences.zh: 惠妃泣訴-{於}-上曰：「太子陰結黨與，將害妾母子，亦指斥至尊。」

translations.literal: Consort Wu Huifei, weeping, complained to the Emperor, saying: "The Crown Prince has secretly formed a faction and will harm me and my son; he also insults Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Huifei tearfully told the Emperor: "The Crown Prince is secretly building a faction and plotting to destroy me and my son—and he even rails against Your Majesty himself."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，以語宰相，欲皆廢之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered; he told the chief ministers and wished to depose them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage, told his chief ministers what she said, and declared he would remove all three princes.

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「陛下踐祚垂三十年，太子諸王不離深宮，日受聖訓，天下之人皆慶陛下享國久長，子孫蕃昌。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling said: "Your Majesty has occupied the throne for nearly thirty years; the Crown Prince and the princes have not left the inner palace, receiving the sage's instruction daily—all under Heaven rejoice that Your Majesty will long hold the state and that descendants will flourish in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling replied: "Your Majesty has ruled for nearly thirty years. The Crown Prince and the royal princes have never left the inner palace; day after day they receive your instruction. All the realm rejoices that your reign will be long and your line will flourish.

sentences.zh: 今三子皆已成人，不聞大過，陛下奈何一旦以無根之語，喜怒之際，盡廢之乎！

translations.literal: Now all three sons have already become adults, and no great faults are heard—how can Your Majesty, in a moment of passion over baseless words, depose them all!
translations.idiomatic: All three are grown men now, and no serious wrongdoing has been reported. How can you, on the spur of anger, act on unsubstantiated gossip and disinherit them all at once!

sentences.zh: 且太子天下本，不可輕搖。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Crown Prince is the root of all under Heaven—it must not be lightly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Crown Prince is the very foundation of the realm. That foundation must not be casually undermined.

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻公-{聽}-驪姬之讒殺申生，三世大亂。

translations.literal: Of old, Duke Xian of Jin listened to Li Ji's slander and killed Shensheng; three generations suffered great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, Duke Xian of Jin heeded Li Ji's calumny and executed Crown Prince Shensheng—and three generations of chaos followed.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝信江充之誣罪戾太子，京城流血。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's false accusation against the Crown Prince Li, and the capital ran with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han trusted Jiang Chong's fabricated charges against Crown Prince Li, and the capital ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝用賈-{後}-之譖廢愍懷太子，中原塗炭。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin took Empress Jia's slander and deposed the Crown Prince Minhuai; the Central Plain was scorched to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin acted on Empress Jia's accusations and deposed Crown Prince Minhuai—and the heartland was laid waste.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝納獨孤-{後}-之言黜太子勇，立煬帝，遂失天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Empress Dugu's words, removed Crown Prince Yong, and installed Emperor Yang—thereby losing all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to Empress Dugu, set aside Crown Prince Yong, and raised Yang Guang to the throne—and in the end lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，不可不愼。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, one cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of history is plain: such a step demands the utmost caution.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲爲此，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must do this, your servant dare not receive the command."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on this course, I cannot in conscience obey such an order.

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 林甫初無所言，退而私謂宦官之貴幸者曰：「此主上家事，何必問外人！」

translations.literal: Li Linfu at first said nothing; on retiring he privately told a favored eunuch: "This is the sovereign's household affair—why must outsiders be consulted!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu said nothing at first. Afterward he took aside a favored eunuch and murmured: "This is a matter for the Son of Heaven's own household. Why consult outsiders at all?"

sentences.zh: 上猶豫未決。

translations.literal: The Emperor hesitated and had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wavered, unable to settle on a decision.

sentences.zh: 惠妃密使官奴牛貴兒謂九齡曰：「有廢必有興，公爲之援，宰相可長處。」

translations.literal: Consort Wu Huifei secretly sent the office slave Niu Guier to tell Zhang Jiuling: "Where there is removal there must be elevation—if you lend support, you may long remain chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Huifei secretly sent her palace attendant Niu Guier to Zhang Jiuling with this offer: "One prince deposed means another raised. Back us, and you can keep your post as chief minister indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 九齡叱之，以其語白上；

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling berated him and reported his words to the Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling rebuked the messenger and reported the overture to the Emperor;

sentences.zh: 上爲之動色，故訖九齡罷相，太子得無動。

translations.literal: the Emperor was moved in countenance on account of this; therefore up until Zhang Jiuling's dismissal from the chief ministership, the Crown Prince remained unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor's expression changed at the news. From that point until Zhang Jiuling was removed from office, the Crown Prince was left unshaken.

sentences.zh: 林甫日夜短九齡-{於}-上，上浸疎之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu day and night spoke ill of Zhang Jiuling before the Emperor; the Emperor gradually grew distant toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu daily poisoned the Emperor's mind against Zhang Jiuling, and the Emperor steadily turned away from him.

sentences.zh: 林甫引蕭炅爲戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: Li Linfu recommended Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had Xiao Jiong appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 炅素不學，嘗對中書侍郎嚴挺之讀「伏-{臘}-」爲「伏獵」。

translations.literal: Jiong had never been studious; once, facing Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Tingzhi, he read "fuxi" (dog days and year-end sacrifice) as "fuxie" (lying in wait to hunt).
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jiong was wholly unlettered. Once, in the presence of Secretariat Vice Director Yan Tingzhi, he misread the phrase for the dog days and the winter sacrifice as "lying in wait to hunt."

sentences.zh: 挺之言-{於}-九齡曰：「省中豈容有『伏獵侍郎』！」

translations.literal: Tingzhi told Zhang Jiuling: "How can the Secretariat tolerate a 'Lying-in-Wait-to-Hunt Vice Minister'!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi complained to Zhang Jiuling: "What kind of Secretariat harbors a 'Lie-in-Wait-to-Hunt Vice Minister'?"

sentences.zh: 由是出炅爲岐州刺史，故林甫怨挺之。

translations.literal: On this account Jiong was sent out as Prefect of Qi Prefecture; therefore Linfu bore resentment toward Tingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On that account Xiao Jiong was posted out as prefect of Qi Prefecture—and from that day Li Linfu nursed a grudge against Yan Tingzhi.

sentences.zh: 九齡與挺之善，欲引以爲相，嘗謂之曰：「李尚書方承恩，足下宜一造門，與之款暱。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling was on good terms with Tingzhi and wished to bring him in as chief minister; he once told him: "Minister Li is now receiving favor—you ought to pay one visit to his door and grow close with him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, who was close to Yan Tingzhi and hoped to see him elevated to chief minister, urged him once: "Li Linfu is in the Emperor's favor. You ought to pay him a visit and cultivate his goodwill.

sentences.zh: 挺之素負氣，薄林甫爲人，竟不之詣；

translations.literal: Tingzhi by nature possessed spirit and looked down on Linfu's character; in the end he did not go to call on him;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi, proud by nature and contemptuous of Li Linfu's character, refused to go.

sentences.zh: 林甫恨之益深。

translations.literal: Linfu hated him all the more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu's hatred only deepened.

sentences.zh: 挺之先娶妻，出之，更嫁蔚州刺史王元琰，元琰坐贓罪下三司按鞫，挺之爲之營解。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had first taken a wife and divorced her; she remarried Wang Yuanyan, Prefect of Yu Prefecture. Yuanyan, on account of a bribery offense, was handed to the Three Offices for investigation and interrogation; Tingzhi worked on his behalf to secure release.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi had divorced his first wife, who later married Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Yu Prefecture. When Wang was charged with graft and investigated by the Three Offices, Yan Tingzhi maneuvered to clear him.

sentences.zh: 林甫因左右使-{於}-禁中白上。

translations.literal: Li Linfu, through attendants, had word sent within the Forbidden City to inform the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu used palace attendants to report this to the Emperor inside the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「挺之爲罪人請屬所由。」

translations.literal: The Emperor told the chief ministers: "Tingzhi pleads on behalf of a criminal and intercedes with the responsible officials."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told his ministers: "Yan Tingzhi has been pulling strings for a convicted criminal.

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「此乃挺之出妻，不宜有情。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling said: "This is Tingzhi's divorced wife—there ought not to be personal feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling replied: "That was his divorced wife. He should feel no lingering obligation.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「雖離乃-{復}-有私。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Though divorced, there is still private feeling."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Even after divorce, the tie of affection remains."

sentences.zh: -{於}-是上積前事，以耀卿、九齡爲阿黨；

translations.literal: On this the Emperor accumulated the previous matters and deemed Yaoqing and Jiuling a partisan clique;
translations.idiomatic: At this the Emperor, adding up earlier grievances, accused Pei Yaoqing and Zhang Jiuling of factionalism;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以耀爲左丞相，九齡爲右丞相，-{並}-罷政事。

translations.literal: on renyin, Yao was made Left Chief Minister, Jiuling Right Chief Minister, and both were dismissed from handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Pei Yaoqing was named Left Chief Minister and Zhang Jiuling Right Chief Minister—but both were stripped of real authority.

sentences.zh: 以林甫兼中書令；

translations.literal: Li Linfu was appointed concurrently as Director of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was additionally given the post of Director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 仙客爲工部尚書、同中書門下三品，鄰朔方節度如故。

translations.literal: Xianke was made Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat of the Third Rank; his command of the Shuofang circuit remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke became Minister of Works with third-rank chancellery status, while retaining his command of the Shuofang frontier circuit.

sentences.zh: 嚴挺之貶洺州刺史，王元琰流嶺南。

translations.literal: Yan Tingzhi was demoted to Prefect of Ming Prefecture; Wang Yuanyan was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi was demoted to prefect of Ming Prefecture; Wang Yuanyan was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 上即位以來，所用之相，姚崇尚通，宋珪尚法，張嘉貞尚吏，張説尚文，李元紘、杜暹尚儉，韓休、張九齡尚直，各其所長也。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor's accession, the chief ministers employed—Yao Chong valued comprehensiveness, Song Jing valued law, Zhang Jiazhen valued administration, Zhang Yue valued letters, Li Yuanhong and Du Xian valued frugality, Han Xiu and Zhang Jiuling valued uprightness—each had his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xuanzong took the throne, each chief minister had been chosen for a distinct strength: Yao Chong for breadth, Song Jing for legal rigor, Zhang Jiazhen for bureaucratic efficiency, Zhang Yue for literary polish, Li Yuanhong and Du Xian for austerity, Han Xiu and Zhang Jiuling for blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 九齡既得罪，自是朝廷之士，皆容身保位，無-{復}-直言。

translations.literal: Once Jiuling had met with offense, from that time court gentlemen all preserved their persons and kept their positions, no longer speaking straight words.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Jiuling's fall, court officials everywhere learned to keep their heads down and hold their tongues.

sentences.zh: 李林甫欲蔽塞人主視-{聽}-，自專大權，明召諸諫官謂曰：「今明主在上，群臣將順之不暇，烏用多言！

translations.literal: Li Linfu wished to block the sovereign's sight and hearing and monopolize great power; he openly summoned the remonstrating officials and said: "Now a bright lord is above; the many ministers are hard pressed to follow in accord—what use is much speech!
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu meant to blind the Emperor to criticism and hold power alone. He summoned the remonstrance officials openly and told them: "We have a wise ruler on the throne. The rest of us can barely keep pace with his wishes—why yap endlessly?

sentences.zh: 諸君不見立仗馬乎？

translations.literal: Do you gentlemen not see the standing-at-attention horses?
translations.idiomatic: Have you never noticed the horses that stand guard at imperial ceremonies?

sentences.zh: 食三品料，一鳴輒斥去，悔之何及！」

translations.literal: They eat third-rank rations; at one neigh they are at once dismissed—what time remains for regret!"
translations.idiomatic: They feed on third-rank rations. One neigh, and they are driven away—too late for regret then!"

sentences.zh: 補闕杜璡嘗上書言事，明日，黜爲下邽令。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Supplement Du Hun once submitted a memorial on affairs; the next day he was demoted to Magistrate of Xi'a County.
translations.idiomatic: When Remonstrance Supplement Du Hun once memorialized the throne, he was the very next day demoted to magistrate of Xi'a County.

sentences.zh: 自是諫爭路絶矣。

translations.literal: From this the path of remonstrance and dispute was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the road to frank counsel was closed for good.

sentences.zh: 牛仙客既爲林甫所引進，專給唯諾而已。

translations.literal: Niu Xianke, having been brought in by Linfu, simply gave assent and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke, Li Linfu's protégé, did nothing in office but nod assent.

sentences.zh: 然二人皆謹守格式，百官遷除，各有常度，雖奇-{才}-異行，不免終老常調；

translations.literal: Yet both men strictly observed regulations and forms; for the hundred officials' transfers and appointments each had its regular measure—even those of exceptional talent and conduct could not avoid ending their lives in ordinary rank;
translations.idiomatic: Yet both men clung rigidly to bureaucratic precedent. Appointments followed fixed rules, so even men of genuine talent and distinction were often condemned to end their careers in routine posts;

sentences.zh: 其以巧諂邪險自進者，則超騰不次，自有它蹊矣。

translations.literal: those who by artful flattery, wickedness, and treachery advanced themselves leapt up out of turn and had other paths of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Men who climbed by flattery and intrigue, by contrast, rocketed past their superiors by altogether different routes.

sentences.zh: 林甫城府深密，人莫窺其際。

translations.literal: Li Linfu's fortified city was deep and sealed; no one could glimpse his boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu's schemes ran deep; no one could see to their bottom.

sentences.zh: 好以甘言啖人，而陰中傷之，不露辭色。

translations.literal: He was fond of feeding people sweet words, yet secretly struck at them, showing neither word nor countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He laced his honeyed words with hidden knives, never betraying a flicker of intent on his face.

sentences.zh: 凡爲上所厚者，始則親結之，及位勢稍逼，輒以計去之。

translations.literal: All whom the Emperor favored—at first he would draw close to them in intimacy; when position and power slightly pressed close, he would immediately by stratagem remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone the Emperor favored, Li Linfu would first befriend. Once that person grew powerful enough to threaten him, he contrived their ruin.

sentences.zh: 雖老-{奸}-巨猾，無能逃其-{術}-者。

translations.literal: Even old schemers and great rogues had none who could escape his techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Even veteran schemers could not elude his methods.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，初置玄學博士，毎歳依明經舉。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Xuanxue Doctorate was first established; each year candidates were selected according to the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the throne first created posts of Doctor of Arcane Learning, with annual recruitment patterned on the Classicist examinations.

sentences.zh: 二月，敕曰：「進士以聲韻爲學，多昧古今；

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict stated: "Jinshi candidates take tonal prosody as their study and are mostly ignorant of antiquity and the present;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, an edict declared: "Jinshi examinees train chiefly in rhyme and tone, and know too little of past and present;

sentences.zh: 明經以貼誦爲功，罕窮旨趣。

translations.literal: Mingjing candidates take pasted recitation as merit and rarely exhaust essential purport.
translations.idiomatic: Classicist candidates memorize by rote and rarely grasp true meaning.

sentences.zh: 自今明經問大義十條，對時務策三首；

translations.literal: From today Mingjing candidates shall be questioned on ten items of great principle and answer three policy essays on current affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Classicists shall be examined on ten questions of principle and required to submit three essays on current affairs;

sentences.zh: 進士試大經十貼。」

translations.literal: Jinshi candidates shall be tested on ten pasted passages from the greater classics."
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi candidates shall be tested on ten pasted passages from the greater classics."

sentences.zh: 戊辰，新羅王興光卒，子承慶襲位。

translations.literal: On wuchen, King Seonggwang of Silla died; his son Seonggyeong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, King Seonggwang of Silla died; his son Seonggyeong succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，幽州節度使張守珪破契丹-{於}-捺祿山。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui of Youzhou defeated the Khitan at Nalushan.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of You Prefecture, routed the Khitans at Mount Nalushan.

sentences.zh: 己亥，河西節度使崔希逸襲吐蕃，破之-{於}-靑海西。

translations.literal: On jihai, Military Commissioner Cui Xiyi of Hexi made a surprise attack on Tibet and defeated them west of Qinghai Lake.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Cui Xiyi, military commissioner of the Hexi circuit, raided Tibet and crushed their forces west of Qinghai Lake.

sentences.zh: 初，希逸遣使謂吐蕃邊將乞力徐曰：「兩國通好，今爲一家，何必更置兵守捉，妨人耕牧！

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiyi sent an envoy to tell the Tibetan frontier general Geluxu: "Our two states are in harmonious relations; we are now one family—why must we again set troops to guard and seize, obstructing people's plowing and pasturing!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Xiyi had sent an envoy to the Tibetan frontier commander Geluxu: "Our two countries are at peace—we are kin now. Why keep armies posted to harass farmers and herdsmen?

sentences.zh: 請皆罷之。」

translations.literal: I ask that we all withdraw them."
translations.idiomatic: Let us pull them all back.

sentences.zh: 乞力徐曰：「常侍忠厚，言必不欺。

translations.literal: Geluxu said: "The Regular Attendant is loyal and thick; his words will surely not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Geluxu replied: "Commissioner Cui is an honest man—I trust he speaks in good faith.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷未必專以邊事相委，萬一有-{奸}-人交-{斗}-其間，掩吾無備，悔之何及！」

translations.literal: Yet the court may not exclusively entrust border affairs to him; in the event some wicked person sets strife between us and catches us unprepared, what time will there be for regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court may not leave all frontier matters entirely in his hands. If some troublemaker sets us at odds and catches us off guard, we will regret it too late!

sentences.zh: 希逸固請，乃刑白狗爲盟，各去守備；

translations.literal: Xiyi pressed insistently; they then cut a white dog to covenant and each removed garrison defenses;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiyi pressed hard. They slaughtered a white dog as oath sacrifice and withdrew their border garrisons on both sides;

sentences.zh: -{於}-是吐蕃畜牧被野。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tibetan herds and flocks covered the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan herds then ranged freely across the open country.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃西撃勃律，勃律來告急。

translations.literal: At that time Tibet struck Bolor in the west; Bolor came to report urgency.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tibet was campaigning west against Bolor, which sent urgent appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 上命吐蕃罷兵，吐蕃不奉詔，遂破勃律；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Tibet to halt troops; Tibet did not receive the edict and thereupon broke Bolor;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Tibet to withdraw, but Tibet ignored the command and overran Bolor;

sentences.zh: 上甚怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 會希逸傔人孫誨入奏事，自欲求功，奏稱吐蕃無備，請掩撃，必大獲。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiyi's personal attendant Sun Hui entered to report affairs; seeking merit for himself, he memorialized that Tibet was unprepared and asked for a surprise attack—great gains were certain.
translations.idiomatic: Around then Cui Xiyi's aide Sun Hui arrived at court on routine business. Hungry for glory, he reported that Tibet lay undefended and urged a surprise raid that would yield rich booty.

sentences.zh: 上命内給事趙惠琮與誨偕往，審察事宜。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Inner Provisioner Zhao Huicong to go together with Hui and examine the state of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Inner Provisioner Zhao Huicong to accompany Sun Hui and assess the situation on the ground.

sentences.zh: 惠琮等至，則矯詔令希逸襲之。

translations.literal: When Huicong and the others arrived, they then forged an edict ordering Xiyi to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, they counterfeited an imperial order commanding Cui Xiyi to attack.

sentences.zh: 希逸不得已，-{發}-兵自涼州南入吐蕃境二千-{餘}--{里}-，至靑海西，與吐蕃戰，大破之，斬首二千-{餘}-級，乞力徐脱身走。

translations.literal: Xiyi had no choice; he raised troops from Liang Prefecture southward into Tibetan territory more than two thousand li, reaching west of Qinghai Lake, fought with Tibet, and inflicted a great defeat—more than two thousand heads cut off; Geluxu escaped by the skin of his body.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiyi had no choice. He marched south from Liangzhou more than two thousand li into Tibetan territory, fought at Qinghai Lake, and won a crushing victory, killing more than two thousand men. Geluxu fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 惠琮、誨皆受厚賞。

translations.literal: Huicong and Hui both received thick rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huicong and Sun Hui were both richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 自是吐蕃-{復}-絶朝貢。

translations.literal: From this Tibet again cut off court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Tibet again ceased sending tribute to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛酉，監察-{御}-史周子諒彈牛仙客非-{才}-，引讖書爲證。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou, Supervising Censor Zhou Ziliang impeached Niu Xianke as lacking talent, citing apocryphal texts as proof.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou, Supervising Censor Zhou Ziliang accused Niu Xianke of being unfit for office, citing prophecy books in evidence.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命左右手暴-{於}-殿庭，絶而-{復}-甦；

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and ordered attendants to expose him publicly in the palace courtyard; he lost consciousness and then revived;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and had attendants beat him savagely in the palace courtyard until he collapsed, then revived him;

sentences.zh: 仍杖之朝堂，流瀼州，至藍田而死。

translations.literal: he was still cudgelled in the audience hall, exiled to Rang Prefecture, and died at Lantian en route.
translations.idiomatic: He was further caned in the audience hall, exiled to Rang Prefecture, and died at Lantian on the way.

sentences.zh: 李林甫言：「子諒，張九齡所-{薦}-也。」

translations.literal: Li Linfu said: "Ziliang was recommended by Zhang Jiuling."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu observed: "Zhou Ziliang was Zhang Jiuling's protégé.

sentences.zh: 甲子，貶九齡荊州長史。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Jiuling was demoted to Chief Secretary of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Zhang Jiuling was demoted to chief secretary of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楊洄又譖太子瑛、鄂王瑤、光王琚，-{雲}-與太子妃兄駙馬薛銹潛構異謀，上召宰相謀之。

translations.literal: Yang Hui again slandered Crown Prince Ying, Prince of E Yao, and Prince of Guang Ju, saying that with the Crown Princess's elder brother the Imperial Son-in-law Xue Xiu they secretly plotted irregular designs; the Emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui again denounced Crown Prince Ying, Prince Yao of E, and Prince Ju of Guang, claiming they were secretly plotting treason with the Crown Prince's brother-in-law, Imperial Son-in-law Xue Xiu. The Emperor summoned his chief ministers to decide the matter.

sentences.zh: 李林甫對曰：「此陛下家事，非臣等所宜豫。」

translations.literal: Li Linfu replied: "This is Your Majesty's household affair—it is not fitting for your servants to take part."
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu answered: "This is Your Majesty's private family matter. It is not for us ministers to meddle.

sentences.zh: 上意乃決。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 乙-{丑}-，使宦者宣-{制}--{於}-宮中，廢瑛、瑤、琚爲庶人，流銹-{於}-瀼州。

translations.literal: On yichou, eunuchs were sent to proclaim the edict within the palace: Ying, Yao, and Ju were deposed as commoners; Xiu was exiled to Rang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, eunuchs proclaimed the edict in the palace: Ying, Yao, and Ju were stripped of rank and reduced to commoners; Xue Xiu was exiled to Rang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瑛、瑤、琚尋賜死城東驛，銹賜死-{於}-藍田。

translations.literal: Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon ordered to death at the Eastern Post Station; Xiu was ordered to death at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ying, Yao, and Ju were granted death at the Eastern Post Station; Xue Xiu was granted death at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 瑤、琚皆好學，有-{才}-識，死不以罪，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Yao and Ju both loved learning and possessed talent and insight; their deaths were not for crimes—all people regretted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Ju were both studious and capable men, executed without just cause—and the whole court mourned them.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，瑛舅家趙氏、妃家薛氏、瑤舅家皇甫氏，坐流貶者數十人，惟瑤妃家韋氏以妃賢得免。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Zhao clan of Ying's maternal uncle's family, the Xue clan of the consort's family, and the Huangfu clan of Yao's maternal uncle's family—those implicated in exile and demotion numbered several tens; only the Wei clan of Yao's consort's family, because the consort was virtuous, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, dozens from the Zhao clan on Ying's mother's side, the Xue clan on the crown princess's side, and the Huangfu clan on Yao's mother's side were exiled or demoted. Only the Wei clan of Prince Yao's consort was spared, because the princess herself was known for virtue.

sentences.zh: 五月，夷州刺史楊浚坐贓當死，上命杖之六十，流古州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Yang Jun, Prefect of Yi Prefecture, on account of bribery deserved death; the Emperor ordered him beaten sixty strokes and exiled to Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Yang Jun, prefect of Yi Prefecture, faced execution for corruption. The Emperor instead ordered sixty strokes of the cudgel and exile to Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左丞相裴耀卿上疎，以爲：「決杖贖死，恩則甚優；

translations.literal: Left Chief Minister Pei Yaoqing submitted a memorial, holding: "Deciding the cudgel to redeem death—the grace is very generous;
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Minister Pei Yaoqing memorialized the throne: "To commute a death sentence to exile after a beating is merciful indeed;

sentences.zh: 解體受笞，事頗爲辱，上可施之徒隸，不當及-{於}-士人。」

translations.literal: dismembering the body to receive the lash—the affair is rather dishonorable; it may be applied to convict slaves—it should not extend to gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: but to bare a man's flesh for flogging is deeply degrading. Such punishment may suit convict laborers; it ought not be inflicted on men of rank.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸未，敕以方隅底定，令中書門下與諸道節度使量軍鎭閒劇利害，審計兵防定額，-{於}-諸色-{-{徴}-}-人及客戸中召募丁壯，長充邊軍，增給田宅，務加優恤。

translations.literal: On guiwei, an edict, because the regions' corners were settled at the bottom, ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery together with the various circuit military commissioners to measure the military garrisons' idle and pressing advantages and harms, examine and calculate fixed quotas for troop defense, and from among persons of various corvée categories and guest households recruit strong young men for long-term service as frontier troops, increase grants of fields and dwellings, and strive to add generous care.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, citing pacification of the realm, an edict directed the Chancellery and the frontier military commissioners to review each garrison's needs, set troop quotas, and recruit able-bodied men from corvée rolls and migrant households for long-term border service—with added grants of farmland and dwellings and generous benefits.

sentences.zh: 辛-{丑}-，上命有司選宗子有-{才}-者，授以-{台}-省及法官、京縣官，敕曰：「違道慢常，義無私-{於}-王法；

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to select talented imperial clansmen and appoint them to Censorate and Secretariat posts and to posts as law officers and capital county officials; an edict stated: "Violating the Way and treating the constant lightly—in righteousness there is no private favor toward royal law;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Emperor ordered officials to select talented members of the imperial clan for posts in the Censorate, Chancellery, courts of justice, and capital counties. The edict read: "Whoever strays from duty shows no favoritism before the law;

sentences.zh: 修身效節，恩豈薄-{於}-它人！

translations.literal: cultivating the person and rendering loyal service—could grace be thinner than toward other men!
translations.idiomatic: but whoever cultivates virtue and serves loyally shall receive no less favor than any other subject!

sentences.zh: 期-{於}-帥先，勵我風俗。」

translations.literal: We expect them to lead first and encourage our customs and manners."
translations.idiomatic: We expect them to lead by example and uplift the manners of the realm."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己卯，大理少卿徐嶠奏：「今歳天下斷死刑五十八，大理獄院，由來相傳殺氣太盛，鳥雀不棲，今有鵲巣其樹。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Qiao memorialized: "This year death sentences throughout the realm numbered fifty-eight. In the Court of Judicial Review's prison courtyard, tradition holds that the killing qi is too strong and birds do not roost—now a magpie has nested in its tree."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao, Vice Director Xu Qiao of the Court of Judicial Review reported: "This year only fifty-eight death sentences were pronounced empire-wide. The prison courtyard of the Review Court has long been said to reek of death—so strongly that birds will not alight there. Yet now a magpie has built its nest in a tree there.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是百官以-{幾}-致刑措，上表稱賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred officials, because punishment was nearly set aside, submitted memorials offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On this the officials, taking it as a sign that capital punishment had nearly been abolished, submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 上歸功宰輔，庚辰，賜李林甫爵晉國公，牛仙客豳國公。

translations.literal: The Emperor attributed the merit to the chief assistants; on gengchen he bestowed on Li Linfu the title Duke of Jin and on Niu Xianke Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor credited his chief ministers. On gengchen he ennobled Li Linfu as Duke of Jin and Niu Xianke as Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 上命李林甫、牛仙客與法官刪修《律令格式》成，九月，壬申，頒行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Li Linfu, Niu Xianke, and law officers to edit and revise the Statutes, Orders, Regulations, and Forms to completion; in the ninth month, on renshen, they were promulgated and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Li Linfu, Niu Xianke, and the legal officers revise the corpus of statutes and administrative codes. In the ninth month, on renshen, the completed code was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 先是，西北邊數十州多宿重兵，地租營田皆不以贍，始用和糴之法。

translations.literal: Prior to this, on the northwest frontier dozens of prefectures maintained large standing garrisons; land tax and military-farm yields were all insufficient to support them, and they began using the hedi method of harmonious grain purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, dozens of northwestern prefectures had kept heavy garrisons on station, yet local rents and army farms could not sustain them. The court therefore introduced government grain purchases at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 有彭果者，因牛仙客獻策，請行糴法-{於}-關中。

translations.literal: There was one Peng Guo who, through Niu Xianke, submitted a plan asking to implement the purchase method in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Peng Guo, acting through Niu Xianke, proposed extending the grain-purchase system to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 戊子，敕以歳稔-{谷}-賤傷農，命增時-{價}-什二三，和糴東、西畿粟各數百萬斛，停今年江、淮所運租。

translations.literal: On wuzi, an edict cited abundant harvests and cheap grain harming farmers; it ordered raising the current price by two or three tenths, harmoniously purchasing several million hu of grain from the eastern and western capital regions, and suspending this year's grain tribute shipments from the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi an edict declared that bumper harvests had driven grain prices so low as to hurt farmers. The court would pay twelve to thirteen percent above market, buy millions of hu of grain from the two capital districts, and halt this year's Yangtze–Huai tribute shipments.

sentences.zh: 自是關中蓄積羨溢，車駕不-{復}-幸東都矣。

translations.literal: From this time Guanzhong's stores overflowed with surplus, and the imperial carriage no longer visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Guanzhong's granaries brimmed with grain, and the Emperor ceased traveling to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，敕河南、北租應輸含嘉、太原倉者，皆留輸本州。

translations.literal: On guisi, an edict ordered that grain rents from Henan and Hebei that were supposed to be delivered to the Hanjia and Taiyuan granaries should all be retained and delivered within their home prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi an edict directed that Henan and Hebei rents bound for the Hanjia and Taiyuan storehouses should instead be kept and delivered locally.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王璵上疎請立靑帝壇以迎春；

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Wang Yu submitted a memorial asking to establish an Azure Emperor altar to welcome spring;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, a grand master in the Directorate of Ceremonies, memorialized the throne proposing an altar to the Azure Emperor for the spring rites;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛-{丑}-，-{制}-自今立春親迎春-{於}-東郊。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, a decree stated that from now on, at the beginning of spring the Emperor would personally welcome spring at the eastern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, a decree ordained that henceforth the Emperor would personally perform the spring welcoming rite at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 時上頗好祀神鬼，故璵專習祠祭之禮以-{干}-時。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor greatly favored sacrificing to spirits and ghosts, so Yu devoted himself to mastering sacrificial ritual to win favor with the times.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had grown fond of spirit worship, and Wang Yu made a specialty of sacrificial ceremony to court imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 上悅之，以爲侍-{御}-史，領祠祭使。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased with him and appointed him Vice Censor, with charge as commissioner for sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Emperor made him a vice censor and put him in charge of state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 璵祈禱或焚紙錢，類巫覡，習禮者羞之。

translations.literal: When Yu prayed he sometimes burned paper money, resembling a shaman; those versed in ritual were ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: In his prayers Yu would burn paper money like a village sorcerer—a practice that embarrassed the ritual specialists.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上幸驪山温泉。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Emperor visited the Hua Mountain hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，還宮。

translations.literal: On yiyou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，開府儀同三司廣平文貞公宋璟薨。

translations.literal: On jichou, Song Jing, Grand General of the Left with Honour Equal to the Three Dukes and Duke Wen Zhen of Guangping, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Song Jing, Duke Wen Zhen of Guangping and honorary equal to the Three Dukes, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙午，惠妃武氏薨，贈謚貞順皇-{后}-。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, Consort Wu Huifei died; she was posthumously honored as Empress Zhenshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, Consort Wu Huifei died and was posthumously ennobled as Empress Zhenshun.

sentences.zh: 是歳，命將作大匠康愆素之東都毀明堂。

translations.literal: That year, the Emperor ordered Chief Palace Architect Kang Yansu to go to the Eastern Capital and dismantle the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court sent Chief Palace Architect Kang Yansu to Luoyang to tear down the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 愆素上言：「毀之勞人，請去上層，卑-{於}-舊九十五尺，仍舊爲-{乾}-元殿。」

translations.literal: Yansu submitted: "Dismantling it will overtax the people. I ask to remove only the upper tiers, make it ninety-five chi lower than before, and restore it as Qianyuan Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yansu argued: "Full demolition would waste labor. Let us strip off the upper stories, lower the structure by ninety-five chi, and restore the old Qianyuan Hall."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 初令庸調租資課皆以土物輸京都。

translations.literal: For the first time it was ordered that corvée, tax-in-kind, rent, asset levies, and miscellaneous dues all be delivered to the capital as local products.
translations.idiomatic: A new rule required corvée payments, grain taxes, rents, asset dues, and miscellaneous levies to be sent to the capital in local goods rather than cash.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，以牛仙客爲侍中。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Niu Xianke was made Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Niu Xianke was appointed chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 丁-{丑}-，上迎氣-{於}-滻水之東。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the Emperor received the seasonal qi east of the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Emperor performed the seasonal welcoming rite east of the Chan River.

sentences.zh: -{制}-邊地長-{-{徴}-}-兵，召募向足，自今鎭兵勿-{復}-遣，在彼者縱還。

translations.literal: An edict: long-term conscription on the frontier, once recruits are sufficient, from now on garrison troops are not to be rotated out again; those already there are permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that frontier districts had filled their quotas through long-term recruitment; henceforth stationed troops would not be replaced by new drafts, and men already serving there might go home.

sentences.zh: 令天下州、縣、裡別置學。

translations.literal: It was ordered that schools be separately established in every prefecture, county, and village throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered schools set up in every prefecture, county, and village district across the empire.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以李林甫領隴右節度副大使，以鄯州都督杜希望知留-{後}-。

translations.literal: On renchen, Li Linfu was made Deputy Military Commissioner of Longyou; Du Xiwang, Military Governor of Shan Prefecture, was made acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Li Linfu took the deputy command of Longyou, while Du Xiwang, governor of Shan Prefecture, served as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，以牛仙客兼河東節度副大使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yimao, Niu Xianke was also made Deputy Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao, Niu Xianke was additionally named deputy commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 己未，葬貞順皇-{后}--{於}-敬陵。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Empress Zhenshun was buried at Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Empress Zhenshun was interred at Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，敕河-{曲}-六州胡坐康待賓散隸諸州者，-{聽}-還故土，-{於}-鹽、夏之間，置宥州以處之。

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict: the Turkic peoples of the six Hexi prefectures implicated in Kang Daibin's rebellion and dispersed among various prefectures were permitted to return to their native lands; You Prefecture was established between Yan and Xia to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu an edict allowed the six Hexi tribes scattered after Kang Daibin's revolt to return home. You Prefecture was created between Yan and Xia to receive them.

sentences.zh: 三月，吐蕃寇河西，節度使崔希逸撃破之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Tibet raided Hexi; Military Commissioner Cui Xiyi defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Tibet invaded Hexi; Cui Xiyi, the military commissioner, routed the raiders.

sentences.zh: 鄯州都督、知隴右留-{後}-杜希望攻吐蕃新城，拔之，以其地爲威戎軍，置兵一千戍之。

translations.literal: Du Xiwang, Military Governor of Shan Prefecture and acting Longyou commander, attacked Tibet's new city, captured it, made the place Weirong Army, and posted a garrison of one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang, governor of Shan and acting Longyou commander, stormed a newly built Tibetan stronghold, seized it, and garrisoned a thousand men there as the Weirong Army.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙酉，李林甫兼河西節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yiyou, Li Linfu also held the Hexi military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on yiyou, Li Linfu was given the Hexi command as well.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以崔希逸爲河南尹。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Cui Xiyi was made Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Cui Xiyi was appointed governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 希逸自念失信-{於}-吐蕃，内懷愧恨，未-{幾}-而卒。

translations.literal: Xiyi brooded over having broken faith with Tibet; inwardly he harbored shame and resentment, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiyi could not forget that he had betrayed Tibet's trust. Shame and bitterness consumed him, and he died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 太子瑛既死，李林甫數勸上立壽王瑁。

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Ying had died, Li Linfu repeatedly urged the Emperor to install Prince Shou Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Crown Prince Ying was dead, Li Linfu pressed repeatedly for Prince Shou Li Mao to be named heir.

sentences.zh: 上以忠王璵年長，且仁孝恭謹，又好學，意欲立之，猶豫歳-{餘}-不決。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Prince Zhong Yu was older and moreover benevolent, filial, reverent, and careful, and also fond of learning, wished to install him, yet hesitated for more than a year without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored Prince Zhong Li Yu—older, dutiful, modest, and studious—but wavered for over a year before choosing.

sentences.zh: 自念春秋浸髙，三子同日誅死，繼嗣未定，常忽忽不樂，寢膳爲之減。

translations.literal: Reflecting that his years were gradually mounting, that three sons had been executed on the same day, and that the succession remained unsettled, he was often listless and unhappy, and his sleep and meals were reduced on its account.
translations.idiomatic: His age was advancing, three sons had died on one day, and still no heir was chosen. He grew restless and morose, eating and sleeping little.

sentences.zh: 髙力士乘間請其故，上曰：「汝，我家老奴，豈不能揣我意！」

translations.literal: Gao Lishi seized an opportune moment to ask the reason. The Emperor said: "You are my family's old slave—can you not guess my mind!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi found a private moment and asked what troubled him. The Emperor said, "You old servant of our house—surely you can read my thoughts!"

sentences.zh: 力士曰：「得非以郎君未定邪？」

translations.literal: Lishi said: "Could it not be because the heir is undecided?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi replied, "Is it not because the succession is still unsettled?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "It is," said the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「大家何必如此虚勞聖心，但推長而立，誰敢-{復}-爭！」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your Majesty, why torment the sacred heart so vainly? Simply install the eldest—who would dare contest again!"
translations.idiomatic: "Then why torment yourself?" Gao Lishi said. "Install the eldest son, and no one will dare object."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝言是也！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your words are right!
translations.idiomatic: "You are right!" said the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 汝言是也！」

translations.literal: Your words are right!"
translations.idiomatic: You are right!"

sentences.zh: 由是遂定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: And with that the choice was made.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，立璵爲太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Yu was installed as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Li Yu was formally named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 辛-{丑}-，以岐州刺史蕭炅爲河西節度使總留-{後}-事，鄯州都督杜希望爲隴右節度使，太-{僕}-卿王昱爲劍南節度使，分道經略吐蕃，仍毀所立赤嶺碑。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Xiao Jiong, Prefect of Qi, was made Hexi Military Commissioner with overall charge of rear-area affairs; Du Xiwang, Military Governor of Shan, was made Longyou Military Commissioner; Wang Yu, Minister of the Imperial Stud, was made Jiannan Military Commissioner; they were to advance against Tibet by separate routes and also destroy the Chiling stele that had been erected.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Xiao Jiong of Qi Prefecture took Hexi command, Du Xiwang took Longyou, and Wang Yu took Jiannan. Each was to strike Tibet along a different route and pull down the Chiling peace monument.

sentences.zh: 突騎施可汗功祿，素廉儉，毎攻戰所得，輒與諸部分之，不留私蓄，由是衆樂爲用。

translations.literal: The Turgesh qaghan Suluo had always been frugal; whenever he gained booty in battle he at once divided it among the tribes, keeping no private store, and on this account the masses were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Suluo, khan of the Turgesh, lived plainly. Every campaign's spoils he shared among his tribesmen and kept nothing for himself, and they fought willingly for him.

sentences.zh: 既尚唐公主，又潛通突厥及吐蕃，突厥、吐蕃各以女妻之。

translations.literal: After he had married a Tang princess, he also secretly communicated with the Turks and Tibet; the Turks and Tibet each gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Though allied to Tang by marriage, he also courted the Turks and Tibetans, taking a princess from each people.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿以三國女爲可敦，又立數子爲-{葉}-護，用度浸廣，由是攻戰所得，不-{復}-更分。

translations.literal: Suluo took women of three states as qatuns and also installed several sons as yabghus; expenditures gradually broadened, and on this account the gains of battle were no longer further divided.
translations.idiomatic: Suluo kept three royal wives and made several sons sub-khans. Expenses mounted, and he ceased sharing war booty with his followers.

sentences.zh: 晩年病風，一手攣縮，諸部離心。

translations.literal: In his later years he fell ill with wind disease; one hand curled and contracted, and the tribes lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he suffered a paralytic stroke that left one hand clenched, and loyalty among the tribes frayed.

sentences.zh: 酋長莫賀達-{干}-、都摩度兩部最強，其部落又分爲黃姓、黑姓，互相乖阻，-{於}-是莫賀達-{干}-勒兵夜襲蘇祿，殺之。

translations.literal: The chieftains Mohedagan and Dumedu were the two strongest factions; their tribes were further divided into Yellow-clan and Black-clan, mutually obstructive; thereupon Mohedagan led troops by night to surprise Suluo and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Two factions led by Mohedagan and Dumedu were strongest, each split between Yellow and Black clans at odds with one another. Mohedagan then struck by night and killed Suluo.

sentences.zh: 都摩度初與莫賀達-{干}-連謀，既而-{復}-與之異，立蘇祿之子骨啜爲吐火仙可汗，以收其-{餘}-衆，與莫賀達-{干}-相攻。

translations.literal: Dumedu at first joined Mohedagan in conspiracy, but afterward again differed from him; he installed Suluo's son Guchuo as qaghan Tuhuoxian to gather the remaining followers, and fought Mohedagan.
translations.idiomatic: Dumedu had plotted with Mohedagan, then turned against him. He set up Suluo's son Guchuo as Khan Tuhuoxian to rally the survivors and warred with Mohedagan.

sentences.zh: 莫賀達-{干}-遣使告磧西節度使蓋嘉運，上命嘉運招集突騎施、拔汗那以西諸國；

translations.literal: Mohedagan sent envoys to inform Gai Jiayun, Military Commissioner of the Western Deserts; the Emperor ordered Jiayun to summon the Turgesh, Ferghana, and all states west of them;
translations.idiomatic: Mohedagan appealed to Gai Jiayun, commissioner of the western frontier. The Emperor ordered Gai to rally the Turgesh, Ferghana, and the kingdoms beyond;

sentences.zh: 吐火仙與都摩度據碎-{葉}-城，黑姓可汗爾微特勒據怛邏斯城，相與連兵以拒唐。

translations.literal: Tuhuoxian and Dumedu held Suyab, the Black-clan qaghan Erweitele held Talas, and together they joined forces to resist Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhuoxian and Dumedu held Suyab; the Black-clan khan Erweitele held Talas. Together they mustered armies against Tang.

sentences.zh: 太子將受冊命，儀注有中嚴、外辦及絳紗袍，太子嫌與至尊同稱，表請易之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was about to receive investiture, the ritual protocol included inner escort, outer preparation, and crimson gauze robes; the crown prince disliked sharing titles with the supreme sovereign and submitted a memorial asking to change them.
translations.idiomatic: As the crown prince's enthronement neared, he objected to ceremonial titles and garments that mirrored the Emperor's—inner escort, outer preparation, and crimson gauze robes—and petitioned for changes.

sentences.zh: 左丞相裴耀卿奏停中嚴，改外辦曰外備，改絳紗袍爲朱明服。

translations.literal: Left Chief Councillor Pei Yaoqing memorialized to stop the inner escort, change outer preparation to outer guard, and change crimson gauze robes to vermilion-bright robes.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Pei Yaoqing proposed abolishing the inner escort, renaming outer preparation as outer guard, and replacing crimson gauze with vermilion-bright robes.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己巳，上-{御}-宣政殿，冊太子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jisi, the Emperor ascended the Xuanzheng Hall and invested the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jisi, the Emperor invested the crown prince in the Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 故事，太子乘輅至殿門。

translations.literal: By precedent, the crown prince rode in the imperial carriage to the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: Customarily the crown prince arrived by imperial carriage at the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 至是，太子不就輅，自其宮歩入。

translations.literal: On this occasion the crown prince did not take the carriage but walked from his palace.
translations.idiomatic: This time he declined the carriage and walked from his own palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，赦天下。

translations.literal: That day, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared the same day.

sentences.zh: 己卯，冊忠王妃韋氏爲太子妃。

translations.literal: On jimao, Consort Wei of Prince Zhong was invested as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Lady Wei, consort of Prince Zhong, was made crown princess.

sentences.zh: 杜希望將鄯州之衆奪吐蕃河橋，-{築}-鹽泉城-{於}-河左，吐蕃-{發}-兵三萬逆戰，希望衆少，不敵，將卒皆懼。

translations.literal: Du Xiwang led the forces of Shan Prefecture to seize a Tibetan river bridge, built Salt Spring City on the river's left bank; Tibet sent thirty thousand troops to meet them in battle. Xiwang's force was few and could not match them; officers and soldiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang led Shan troops to capture a Tibetan bridge and build Salt Spring City on the near bank. Tibet answered with thirty thousand men. Outnumbered, Du Xiwang's soldiers were terrified.

sentences.zh: 左威衞郎將王忠嗣帥所部先犯其陳，所向-{辟}-易，殺數百人，虜陳亂。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongsi, Captain of the Left Guard, led his unit first to strike their battle line; wherever he went he cleared a path, killed several hundred men, and the barbarian formation fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongsi of the Left Guard led his detachment in the first charge, cutting through the enemy line, slaying hundreds and throwing the Tibetan ranks into confusion.

sentences.zh: 希望縱兵乘之，虜遂大敗。

translations.literal: Xiwang unleashed his troops to press the advantage, and the barbarians were thoroughly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang then ordered a general advance, and the Tibetans were routed.

sentences.zh: 置鎭西軍-{於}-鹽泉。

translations.literal: The Pacifying-the-West Army was established at Salt Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The court established the Pacifying-the-West Army at Salt Spring.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣以功遷左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Zhongsi, for his merit, was promoted to General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat Wang Zhongsi was promoted to general of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛巳，勃海王武藝卒，子欽茂立。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinsi, King Wuyi of Bohai died; his son Qinmao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinsi, King Wuyi of Bohai died and was succeeded by his son Qinmao.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the bingshen new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day of the cycle (bingshen), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 初，儀鳳中，吐蕃陷安戎城而據之，其地險要，唐屢攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Yifeng era, Tibet captured and held Anrong City; the terrain was strategically vital, and Tang repeatedly attacked without success.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng reign Tibet had seized Anrong City, a fortress Tang had assaulted many times in vain.

sentences.zh: 劍南節度使王昱-{築}-兩城-{於}-其側，頓軍蒲婆嶺下，運資糧以逼之。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, Military Commissioner of Jiannan, built two cities beside it, encamped troops below Pupo Ridge, and transported provisions to press the place.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan commissioner Wang Yu built twin forts nearby, camped on Pupo Ridge, and pushed supplies forward to choke the garrison.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大-{發}-兵救安戎城，昱衆大敗，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Tibet sent a large force to relieve Anrong City; Yu's army was thoroughly defeated, and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet marched a great army to relieve the city. Wang Yu's force was shattered and thousands perished.

sentences.zh: 昱脱身走，糧仗軍資皆棄之。

translations.literal: Yu escaped with his body, abandoning grain, weapons, and military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu fled alive, leaving grain, arms, and equipment behind.

sentences.zh: 貶昱括州刺史，再貶髙要尉而死。

translations.literal: Yu was demoted to Prefect of Kuozhou, demoted again to Captain of Gaoyao, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou, then again to magistrate of Gaoyao, where he died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，冊南詔蒙歸義爲-{雲}-南王。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Piluoge of Nanzhao was invested as King of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Meng Guigyi of Nanzhao was enfeoffed as King of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 歸義之先本哀牢夷，地居姚州之西，東南接交趾，西北接吐蕃。

translations.literal: Guigyi's ancestors were originally Ailao barbarians; their land lay west of Yao Prefecture, touching Jiaozhi to the southeast and Tibet to the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Guigyi's people were Ailao tribesmen west of Yao Prefecture, bordered by Jiaozhi in the southeast and Tibet in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 蠻語謂王曰詔，先有六詔：曰蒙-{捨}-，曰蒙越，曰越析，曰浪穹，曰樣備，曰越澹，兵力相埒，莫能相壹；

translations.literal: In the barbarian tongue a king is called zhao; there were originally six zhao: called Mengshe, Mengyue, Yuexi, Langqiong, Yangbei, and Yueta; their military strength was equal, and none could unify the others;
translations.idiomatic: In their language "zhao" meant king. Six kingdoms—Mengshe, Mengyue, Yuexi, Langqiong, Yangbei, and Yueta—matched one another in power and none could dominate the rest;

sentences.zh: 歴代因之以分其勢。

translations.literal: successive dynasties relied on this to divide their strength.
translations.idiomatic: successive dynasties had deliberately kept them divided.

sentences.zh: 蒙-{捨}-最在南，故謂之南詔。

translations.literal: Mengshe was farthest south, and therefore was called Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshe lay southernmost, hence the name Nanzhao, the Southern Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 髙宗時，蒙-{捨}-細奴邏初入朝。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong era, Xinuluo of Mengshe first came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Mengshe's chief Xinuluo first visited the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 細奴邏生邏盛，邏盛生盛邏皮，盛邏皮生皮邏閣。

translations.literal: Xinuluo begot Luosheng; Luosheng begot Shengluopi; Shengluopi begot Piluoge.
translations.idiomatic: The line ran Xinuluo to Luosheng, Luosheng to Shengluopi, Shengluopi to Piluoge.

sentences.zh: 皮邏閣浸強大，而五詔微弱；

translations.literal: Piluoge gradually grew powerful while the five zhao weakened;
translations.idiomatic: Piluoge grew ever stronger as the other five kingdoms waned;

sentences.zh: 會有破渳河蠻之功，乃賂王昱，求合六詔爲一。

translations.literal: when he had the achievement of defeating the Mihe River barbarians, he bribed Wang Yu and asked to unite the six zhao into one.
translations.idiomatic: after crushing the Mihe River tribes he bribed Wang Yu to petition for unification of the six zhao.

sentences.zh: 昱爲之奏請，朝遷許之，仍賜名歸義。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized on his behalf; the court approved and moreover bestowed the name Guigyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu forwarded the request; the court agreed and granted Piluoge the name Guigyi.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是以兵威脅服群蠻，不從者滅之，遂撃破吐蕃，徙居大和城；

translations.literal: Thereupon by military might he coerced the barbarian tribes into submission; those who would not obey he destroyed; he then defeated Tibet and moved his seat to Dali City;
translations.idiomatic: He then bullied neighboring tribes into submission, annihilating the recalcitrant, broke Tibetan power, and moved his capital to Dali;

sentences.zh: 其-{後}-卒爲邊患。

translations.literal: afterward he ultimately became a frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: in time he would become a scourge on the border.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，上幸驪山温泉，壬辰，上還宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the Emperor visited the Hua Mountain hot springs; on renchen he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin the Emperor went to the Mount Li hot springs; on renchen he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歳，-{於}-西京、東都往來之路，作行宮千-{餘}-間。

translations.literal: That year, along the road between the Western and Eastern capitals, more than a thousand traveling palaces were built.
translations.idiomatic: That year over a thousand way stations were built along the route between Chang'an and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 分左右羽林置龍武軍，以萬騎營隸焉。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Forest guards were divided to establish the Dragon Martial Army, with the Ten Thousand Horsemen Camp subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Left and Right Forest guards the court formed the Dragon Martial Army, subordinating the Ten Thousand Horsemen Camp to it.

sentences.zh: 潤州刺史齊澣奏：「舊自瓜歩濟江，迂六十-{里}-。

translations.literal: Qi Huan, Prefect of Run, memorialized: "Formerly, crossing the Yangtze from Guabu made a detour of sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: Run Prefect Qi Huan reported: "The old crossing from Guabu required a sixty-li roundabout.

sentences.zh: 請自京口埭下直濟江，穿伊婁河二十五-{里}-即達揚子縣，立伊婁埭。」

translations.literal: I ask to cross the Yangtze directly below the Jingkou dam, cut through the Yilou River for twenty-five li to reach Yangzi County, and establish the Yilou dam."
translations.idiomatic: I propose a direct crossing below the Jingkou dam, a twenty-five-li canal through the Yilou River to Yangzi County, and a new Yilou dam."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，命隴右節度大使榮王琬自至本道巡按處置諸軍，選募關内、河東壯士三五萬人，詣隴右防遏，至秋末無寇，-{聽}-還。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renyin, Prince Rong Wan, Grand Military Commissioner of Longyou, was ordered to go in person to his circuit to inspect and dispose of the armies, select and recruit thirty to fifty thousand strong men from Guannei and Hedong, send them to Longyou for defense, and if by the end of autumn there were no raids, they were permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renyin Prince Rong Li Wan, Longyou commissioner, was sent to inspect frontier armies and recruit thirty to fifty thousand men from Guannei and Hedong for garrison duty in Longyou, to be released home if no enemy appeared by autumn's end.

sentences.zh: 群臣請加尊號曰聖文；

translations.literal: The hundred officials asked to add the honorific title Shengwen;
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers petitioned to add the honorific "Sagely and Cultured";

sentences.zh: 二月，己巳，許之，因赦天下，免百姓今年田租。

translations.literal: in the second month, on jisi, this was granted; a general amnesty was proclaimed, and this year's field tax for the common people was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on jisi, the title was granted, an amnesty declared, and the year's land tax forgiven.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸酉，敕：「諸陰陽-{術}-數，自非婚喪-{卜}-擇，皆禁之。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, an edict: "All yin-yang arts and numerology, except for divination at weddings and funerals, are forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, an edict banned yin-yang divination and occult arts except for wedding and funeral portents."

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，以牛仙客爲兵部尚書兼侍中，李林甫爲吏部尚書兼中書令，總文武選事。

translations.literal: On jichou, Niu Xianke was made Minister of War and Chief Councillor; Li Linfu was made Minister of Personnel and Director of the Secretariat; together they oversaw civil and military selection.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Niu Xianke became minister of war and chief councillor, Li Linfu minister of personnel and director of the secretariat; together they controlled all appointments.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸酉，以-{御}-史大夫李-{適}-之兼幽州節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiyou, Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi was also made Military Commissioner of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiyou, Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi was additionally named commissioner of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 幽州將趙堪、白眞阤羅矯節度使張守珪之命，使平盧軍使烏知義邀撃叛奚-{餘}-黨-{於}-橫水之北；

translations.literal: The Youzhou generals Zhao Kan and Bai Zhentuoluo, forging Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui's orders, sent Pinglu Army commander Wu Zhiyi to intercept the remnant Xi rebels north of Hengshui;
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou officers Zhao Kan and Bai Zhentuoluo forged orders in Zhang Shougui's name, dispatching Wu Zhiyi of the Pinglu Army to attack Xi rebels north of the Heng River;

sentences.zh: 知義不從，白眞阤羅矯稱-{制}-指以迫之。

translations.literal: Zhiyi would not obey; Bai Zhentuoluo falsely claimed an imperial edict to force him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhiyi refused, so Bai Zhentuoluo pretended the command came straight from the throne.

sentences.zh: 知義不得已出師，與虜遇，先勝-{後}-敗；

translations.literal: Zhiyi, having no choice, took the field; he met the barbarians, was victorious at first and afterward defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Compelled to march, Wu Zhiyi met the enemy, won the opening clash, then lost;

sentences.zh: 守珪隱其敗狀，以克獲聞。

translations.literal: Shougui concealed the defeat and reported a capture victory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui hid the defeat and reported a triumph.

sentences.zh: 事頗洩，上令内謁者監牛仙童作察之。

translations.literal: The matter leaked considerably; the Emperor ordered Palace Gentleman-attendant Supervisor Niu Xiantong to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Word leaked out, and the Emperor ordered the palace attendant-supervisor Niu Xiantong to look into it.

sentences.zh: 守珪重賂仙童，歸罪-{於}-白眞阤羅，逼令自縊死。

translations.literal: Shougui heavily bribed Xiantong, shifted the blame onto Bai Zhentuoluo, and forced him to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui bribed Niu Xiantong lavishly, pinned the fault on Bai Zhentuoluo, and drove him to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 仙童有寵-{於}-上，衆宦官疾之，共-{發}-其事。

translations.literal: Xiantong had favor with the Emperor; the eunuchs resented him and jointly exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Favored at court, Niu Xiantong was hated by the other eunuchs, who together revealed the case.

sentences.zh: 上怒，甲戌，命楊思勗杖殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged; on jiaxu he ordered Yang Sixun to beat him to death with clubs.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, on jiaxu the Emperor ordered Yang Sixun to club him to death.

sentences.zh: 思勗縛格，杖之數百，刳取其心，割其肉啖之。

translations.literal: Sixun bound him in restraint, beat him several hundred strokes, cut open his chest and took his heart, sliced his flesh and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sixun trussed him, flogged him hundreds of times, cut out his heart, and ate pieces of his flesh.

sentences.zh: 守珪坐貶括州刺史。

translations.literal: Shougui was demoted to Prefect of Kuozhou on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 太子太師蕭-{嵩}-嘗賂仙童以城南良田數頃，李林甫-{發}-之，-{嵩}-坐貶靑州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Xiao Song had once bribed Xiantong with several qing of fine farmland south of the city; Li Linfu exposed it, and Song was demoted to Prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xiao Song had once given Niu Xiantong several plots of southern farmland; when Li Linfu exposed the bribe, Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙亥，磧西節度使蓋嘉運擒突騎施可汗吐火仙。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yihai, Gai Jiayun, Military Commissioner of Qixi, captured Tuhuoxian, khan of the Turgish.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yihai, Qixi commissioner Gai Jiayun captured the Turgish khan Tuhuoxian.

sentences.zh: 嘉運攻碎-{葉}-城，吐火仙出戰，敗走，擒之-{於}-賀邏嶺。

translations.literal: Jiayun attacked Suiye city; Tuhuoxian came out to fight, was defeated and fled, and was captured at Heluo Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Jiayun took Suiye; Tuhuoxian fought, lost, fled, and was taken at Heluo Ridge.

sentences.zh: 分遣疎勒鎭守使夫蒙靈察與拔汗那王阿悉爛達-{干}-潛引兵突入怛邏斯城，擒黑姓可汗爾微，遂入曳建城，取交河公主，悉收散-{發}-之民數萬以與拔汗那王，威震西陲。

translations.literal: He separately sent Fumeng Lingcha, garrison commander of Kashgar, and the Ferghana king Asilanda to secretly lead troops into Talas city, capturing the Heixing khan Erwei; they then entered Yejian city, took Princess Jiaohe, and completely collected and sent tens of thousands of scattered people to give to the Ferghana king, shaking the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Kashgar garrison commander Fumeng Lingcha and the Ferghana king Asilanda to steal into Talas, seize the Heixing khan Erwei, enter Yejian, recover Princess Jiaohe, and gather tens of thousands of displaced subjects for the Ferghana king—striking terror across the western marches.

sentences.zh: 壬午，吐蕃寇白草、安人等軍，隴右節度使蕭炅撃破之。

translations.literal: On renwu, Tibet raided the Baicao and Anren garrisons; Xiao Jiong, Military Commissioner of Longyou, defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Tibet attacked the Baicao and Anren garrisons; Longyou commissioner Xiao Jiong routed them.

sentences.zh: 甲申，追謚孔子爲文宣王。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Confucius was posthumously ennobled as King Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Confucius was posthumously titled King Wenxuan, "Spreading Culture."

sentences.zh: 先是，祀先聖先師，周公南向，孔子東向坐。

translations.literal: Previously, when sacrificing to the Sage and Teacher, the Duke of Zhou faced south and Confucius sat facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at rites for the sage and his teacher, the Duke of Zhou faced south while Confucius sat facing east.

sentences.zh: -{制}-：「自今孔子南向坐，被王者之服，釋奠用宮懸。」

translations.literal: An edict: "From now on Confucius shall sit facing south, wear the robes of a king, and the libation sacrifice shall use full palace music."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that henceforth Confucius would face south in kingly robes, with full court music at the libation rite.

sentences.zh: 追贈弟子皆爲公、侯、伯。

translations.literal: His disciples were posthumously ennobled as dukes, marquises, and earls.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples were posthumously ennobled as dukes, marquises, and earls.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，處木昆、鼠尼施、弓月等諸部先隸突騎施者，皆帥衆内附，仍請徙居安西管内。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuwu, the Chumukun, Shunishi, Gongyue, and other tribes formerly subject to the Turgish all led their people to submit and still asked to relocate within Anxi command.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuwu, the Chumukun, Shunishi, Gongyue, and other tribes once under the Turgish all submitted with their followers and petitioned to move into Anxi territory.

sentences.zh: 太子更名紹。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince changed his personal name to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took the new personal name Shao.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳，改修東都明堂。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the Bright Hall of the Eastern Capital was renovated.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, work began on renovating the Eastern Capital's Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，上幸驪山温泉；

translations.literal: On bingxu the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛-{丑}-，還宮。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on xinchou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on xinchou, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，明堂成。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Bright Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Bright Hall was finished.

sentences.zh: 劍南節度使張宥，文吏不習軍旅，悉以軍政委團練副使章仇兼瓊。
