translations.literal: Zhang You, Military Commissioner of Jiannan, was a civil official unversed in military affairs and entirely entrusted military affairs to training commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan commissioner Zhang You was a civilian with no taste for soldiering and handed all military duties to his deputy Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊入奏事，盛言安戎城可取，上悅之。

translations.literal: Jianqiong came to court to report and greatly declared that Anrong city could be taken; the Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong came to court and assured the Emperor that Anrong could be seized; the throne was delighted.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以宥爲光祿卿。

translations.literal: On dingsi You was made Minister of Court Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Zhang You was made minister of court banquets.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以兼瓊爲劍南節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jianqiong was made Military Commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhang Qiu Jianqiong became commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 初，睿宗喪既除，祫-{於}-太廟；

translations.literal: At first, after Emperor Ruizong's mourning period had ended, a combined seasonal rite was performed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ruizong's mourning ended, a combined temple rite was held;

sentences.zh: 自是三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: from then on there was a combined rite every three years and a grand seasonal rite every five years.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter a combined sacrifice came every three years and a grand seasonal sacrifice every five.

sentences.zh: 是歳，夏既禘，冬又當祫。

translations.literal: That year, after the summer grand rite, winter again fell due for the combined rite.
translations.idiomatic: That year the summer grand rite had just been performed when winter also called for the combined ceremony.

sentences.zh: 太常議以爲祭數則瀆，請停今年祫祭，自是通計五年一祫、一禘；

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonials judged that too many sacrifices would be profanation and asked to suspend this year's combined rite; from then on both would be counted together as one combined rite and one grand rite every five years;
translations.idiomatic: The court of rites held that too many offerings would profane the spirits and asked to skip the winter combined rite, fixing both ceremonies once every five years;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，上幸驪山温泉；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 庚子，還宮。

translations.literal: on gengzi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on gengzi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 二月，荊州長史張九齡卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhang Jiuling, Regional Commander of Jingzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhang Jiuling, regional commander of Jingzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 上雖以九齡忤旨逐之，然終愛重其人，毎宰相-{薦}-士，輒問曰：「風度得如九齡不？」

translations.literal: Although the Emperor had banished Jiuling for opposing his will, he still cherished the man to the end; whenever a chief minister recommended a scholar, he would ask: "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?"
translations.idiomatic: Though he had exiled Jiuling for crossing him, the Emperor still treasured him; whenever a minister proposed a candidate, he asked, "Does his grace equal Jiuling's?"

sentences.zh: 三月，丁亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dinghai, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dinghai, the new moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 章仇兼瓊潛與安戎城中吐蕃翟都局及維州別駕董承晏結謀，使局開門引内唐兵，盡殺吐蕃將卒，使監察-{御}-史許遠將兵守之。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiu Jianqiong secretly plotted with the Tibetan officer Zhuduju in Anrong city and Weizhou Vice-Prefect Dong Chengyan, making Ju open the gate and admit Tang troops inside, killing all the Tibetan officers and soldiers, and sending Supervising Censor Xu Yuan with troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiu Jianqiong secretly allied with the Tibetan officer Zhuduju in Anrong and Weizhou vice-prefect Dong Chengyan; Ju opened the gates to Tang troops, who slaughtered the garrison, and Supervising Censor Xu Yuan was left to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 遠，敬宗之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan was the great-grandson of Xu Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was the great-grandson of Xu Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，蓋嘉運入獻捷。

translations.literal: On jiayin Gai Jiayun came to court to present his victory.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Gai Jiayun presented his victory at court.

sentences.zh: 上赦吐火仙罪，以爲左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Tuhuoxian's crime and made him General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Tuhuoxian and appointed him general of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉運請立阿史那懷道之子昕爲十姓可汗；

translations.literal: Jiayun asked to install Xin, son of Ashina Huaidao, as khan of the Ten Surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Gai Jiayun asked to install Ashina Huaidao's son Xin as khan of the Ten Surnames;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛未，以昕妻李氏爲交河公主。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei, Xin's wife Lady Li was made Princess Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei, Xin's wife Lady Li was named Princess Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 六月，吐蕃圍安戎城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Tibet besieged Anrong city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Tibet laid siege to Anrong.

sentences.zh: 上嘉蓋嘉運之功，以爲河西、隴右節度使，使之經略吐蕃。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Gai Jiayun's achievement and made him Military Commissioner of Hexi and Longyou, sending him to manage operations against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rewarded Gai Jiayun with joint command of Hexi and Longyou to conduct operations against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 嘉運恃恩流連，不時-{發}-。

translations.literal: Jiayun, relying on imperial favor, lingered on and did not set out on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Basking in imperial favor, Gai Jiayun dallied and would not depart on time.

sentences.zh: 左丞相裴耀卿上疎，以爲：「臣近與嘉運同班，觀其舉措，誠勇烈有-{餘}-，然言氣矜誇，恐難成事。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Pei Yaoqing submitted a memorial, saying: "I recently sat in the same court session as Jiayun and observed his conduct: he truly has more than enough courage and fierceness, yet his words and bearing are arrogant and boastful—I fear he will be hard put to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Pei Yaoqing memorialized: "I recently sat with Gai Jiayun in court; he is plainly brave, yet his speech is proud and swaggering—I doubt he will succeed.

sentences.zh: 昔莫敖忸-{於}-蒲騷之役，卒喪楚師；

translations.literal: In olden days the Mo'ao was bashful at the battle of Pusao and in the end lost the Chu army;
translations.idiomatic: Once a Mo'ao hesitated before the battle of Pusao and lost the Chu army;

sentences.zh: 今嘉運有驕敵之色，臣竊憂之。

translations.literal: now Jiayun has the look of one who despises the enemy—I am privately worried.
translations.idiomatic: now Gai Jiayun wears the face of a man who scorns his foe—I am deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 況防秋非遠，未言-{發}-日，若臨事始去，則吏卒尚未相識，何以-{制}-敵！

translations.literal: Moreover the autumn defense is not far off, and no day of departure has yet been named; if he only leaves when the crisis comes, officers and soldiers will not yet know one another—how can they control the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Autumn defense is near, yet no departure date is set; if he waits until battle is joined, his men will be strangers to one another—how can they face the enemy!

sentences.zh: 且將軍受命，鑿凶門而出；

translations.literal: Moreover, when a general accepts command he should pass through the ominous gate and take the field;
translations.idiomatic: A general taking command should march at once through the gate of ill omen;

sentences.zh: 今乃酣宴朝夕，殆非憂國愛人之心。

translations.literal: now he feasts morning and night—hardly the heart of one who worries for the state and loves the people.
translations.idiomatic: instead he feasts day and night—hardly the mind of a man who loves realm and people.

sentences.zh: 若不可改易，宜速遣進塗，仍乞聖恩嚴加訓勵。」

translations.literal: If the appointment cannot be changed, he should be urgently sent on his way, and I still beg the sage favor to admonish him sternly."
translations.idiomatic: If the appointment cannot be altered, send him off at once, and grant stern imperial admonishment."

sentences.zh: 上乃趣嘉運行。

translations.literal: The Emperor then pressed Jiayun to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then pressed Gai Jiayun to march.

sentences.zh: 已而嘉運竟無功。

translations.literal: Before long Jiayun in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In time Gai Jiayun accomplished nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，甲戌，幽州奏破奚、契丹。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiayu, Youzhou reported defeating the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiayu, Youzhou reported victories over the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，上幸驪山温泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，還宮。

translations.literal: on xinsi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on xinsi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇安戎城及維州；

translations.literal: Tibet raided Anrong city and Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet attacked Anrong and Weizhou;

sentences.zh: -{發}-關中強騎救之，吐蕃引去。

translations.literal: elite cavalry from Guanzhong were dispatched to rescue them, and Tibet withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: elite Guanzhong cavalry were sent to the rescue, and Tibet withdrew.

sentences.zh: 更命安戎城曰平戎。

translations.literal: Anrong city was renamed Pingrong.
translations.idiomatic: Anrong was renamed Pingrong, "Pacifying the Barbarians."

sentences.zh: 十一月，罷牛仙客朔方、河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Niu Xianke was removed as Military Commissioner of Shuofang and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Niu Xianke was dismissed as commissioner of Shuofang and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 突騎施莫賀達-{干}-聞阿史那昕爲可汗，怒曰：「首誅蘇祿，我之謀也；

translations.literal: Mohedagan of the Turgish, hearing that Ashina Xin had been made khan, said in anger: "The first to be executed for plotting against Suolu was at my counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Mohedagan of the Turgish, learning Ashina Xin had been made khan, raged: "I was the one who plotted to kill Suolu first;

sentences.zh: 今立史昕，何以賞我？」

translations.literal: now you install Xin of the Ashina—how will you reward me?"
translations.idiomatic: now you raise Xin of the Ashina line—where is my reward?"

sentences.zh: 遂帥諸部叛。

translations.literal: He then led the various tribes in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his clans in revolt.

sentences.zh: 上乃立莫賀達-{干}-爲可汗，使統突騎施之衆，命蓋嘉運招諭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then installed Mohedagan as khan, making him command the Turgish host, and ordered Gai Jiayun to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then named Mohedagan khan over the Turgish and ordered Gai Jiayun to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，莫賀達-{干}-降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Mohedagan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Mohedagan submitted.

sentences.zh: 金城公主薨；

translations.literal: Princess Jincheng died;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jincheng died;

sentences.zh: 吐蕃告喪，且請和，上不許。

translations.literal: Tibet announced the mourning and also asked for peace; the Emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent word of mourning and sought peace; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是歳，天下縣千五百七十三，戸八百四十一萬二千八百七十一，口四千八百一十四萬三千六百九。

translations.literal: That year throughout the realm there were 1,573 counties, 8,412,871 households, and 48,143,609 persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the empire counted 1,573 counties, 8,412,871 households, and 48,143,609 people.

sentences.zh: 西京、東都米斛直錢不滿二百，絹匹亦如之。

translations.literal: In the Western and Eastern capitals the price of a hu of rice was less than two hundred cash, and a bolt of silk was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In the two capitals grain cost less than two hundred cash per hu, silk the same.

sentences.zh: 海内富安，行者雖萬-{里}-不持寸兵。

translations.literal: Within the seas there was wealth and peace; travelers even ten thousand li went without carrying so much as a short weapon.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was prosperous and secure; a man might travel ten thousand li without bearing a blade.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，上幸驪山温泉。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，-{制}-：「承前諸州饑饉，皆待奏報，然始開倉賑給。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict: "Previously, when various prefectures suffered famine, they all waited for a memorial report and only then opened the granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou an edict declared: "When famine struck, prefectures had to wait for memorial approval before opening granaries.

sentences.zh: 道路悠遠，何救懸絶！

translations.literal: The roads are long and far—how can that save those hanging by a thread!
translations.idiomatic: Roads are long—what hope for those already starving!

sentences.zh: 自今委州縣長官與採訪使量事給訖奏聞。」

translations.literal: From now on let the prefecture and county magistrates together with the inspection commissioners measure the need, distribute relief, and then report."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth let local magistrates and inspection commissioners distribute grain as needed and report afterward."

sentences.zh: 庚子，上還宮。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 上夢玄元皇帝告-{云}-：「吾有像在京城西南百-{餘}--{里}-，汝遣人求之，吾當與汝興慶宮相見。」

translations.literal: The Emperor dreamed that the Dark Primordial Emperor told him: "I have an image more than a hundred li southwest of the capital; send men to seek it, and I shall meet you at Xingqing Palace."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dreamed the Dark Primordial Lord said: "My statue lies more than a hundred li southwest of the capital; send men to find it, and I will meet you at Xingqing Palace."

sentences.zh: 上遣使求得之-{於}-盩厔樓觀山間。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys who found it among the mountains at Louguan in Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys found it in the mountains at Louguan in Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏四月，迎置興慶宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the intercalary fourth month, it was welcomed and installed at Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of summer it was brought to Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，命畫玄元眞容，分置諸州開元觀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he ordered portraits of the Dark Primordial Lord painted and distributed to Kaiyuan temples in the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he had portraits of the Dark Primordial Lord painted and sent to Kaiyuan temples in every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月，吐蕃四十萬衆入寇，至安仁軍，渾崖峰騎將臧希液帥衆五千撃破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month four hundred thousand Tibetans invaded as far as Anren Army; Zang Xiye, cavalry commander of Hunya Peak, led five thousand men and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month four hundred thousand Tibetans invaded to Anren Army; Zang Xiye of Hunya Peak led five thousand horsemen and routed them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅，突厥遣使來告登利可汗之喪。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the Turks sent envoys to announce the death of Khan Tengli.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, Turk envoys announced the death of Khan Tengli.

sentences.zh: 初，登利從叔二人，分典兵馬，號左、右殺。

translations.literal: At first Tengli had two younger uncles who separately commanded troops and horses, styled the Left and Right Sagha.
translations.idiomatic: Tengli's two younger uncles had each commanded troops, styled the Left and Right Sagha.

sentences.zh: 登利患兩殺之專，與其母謀，誘右殺，斬之，自將其衆。

translations.literal: Tengli resented the two Saghas' monopoly of power; with his mother he plotted, lured the Right Sagha, and beheaded him, then personally led his host.
translations.idiomatic: Tengli resented their monopoly of power; with his mother he lured and killed the Right Sagha, then took command himself.

sentences.zh: 左殺判闕特勒兵攻登利，殺之，立毘伽可汗之子爲可汗；

translations.literal: The Left Sagha Panguo Tegli attacked Tengli with troops, killed him, and installed Bili Khan's son as khan;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Sagha Panguo Tegli attacked and killed Tengli, installing Bili Khan's son as khan;

sentences.zh: 俄爲骨咄-{葉}-護所殺，更立其弟；

translations.literal: before long he was killed by Gutu Ye Hu, who installed his younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: soon Gutu Ye Hu killed him and raised his brother;

sentences.zh: 尋又殺之，骨咄-{葉}-護自立爲可汗。

translations.literal: not long after he too was killed, and Gutu Ye Hu installed himself as khan.
translations.idiomatic: before long he too was killed, and Gutu Ye Hu declared himself khan.

sentences.zh: 上以突厥内亂，癸酉，命左羽林將軍孫老奴招諭回紇、葛邏祿、拔悉密等部落。

translations.literal: Because the Turks were in internal disorder, on guiyou the Emperor ordered Left Forest Guard General Sun Laonu to win over the Uighurs, Karluk, Basmyl, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: With the Turks torn by civil strife, on guiyou the Emperor ordered General Sun Laonu of the Left Forest Guard to win over the Uighurs, Karluk, Basmyl, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，東都洛水溢，溺死者千-{餘}-人。

translations.literal: On yihai the Luo River in the Eastern Capital overflowed; more than a thousand people drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Luo River flooded the Eastern Capital, drowning more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 平盧兵馬使安祿山，傾巧，善事人，人多譽之。

translations.literal: An Lushan, military envoy of Pinglu, was clever and skilled at pleasing people; many praised him.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan, Pinglu military envoy, was cunning and ingratiating; many sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 上左右至平盧者，祿山皆厚賂之，由是上益以爲賢。

translations.literal: Everyone from the Emperor's attendants down to those who reached Pinglu—Lushan lavishly bribed them all; thereby the Emperor came to regard him as even more worthy.
translations.idiomatic: From the Emperor's attendants to every visitor at Pinglu, An Lushan lavished gifts; the throne therefore thought him ever more able.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史中丞張利貞爲河北採訪使，至平盧。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zhang Lizhen was made Hebei Inspection Commissioner and reached Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Zhang Lizhen became Hebei inspection commissioner and visited Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 祿山-{曲}-事利貞，乃至左右皆有賂。

translations.literal: Lushan curried favor with Lizhen to the point that even those at his side all received bribes.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan fawned on Zhang Lizhen until even his attendants were paid off.

sentences.zh: 利貞入奏，盛稱祿山之美。

translations.literal: Lizhen came to court to report and greatly praised Lushan's virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lizhen returned to court and extolled An Lushan's merits.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙未，以祿山爲營州都督，充平盧軍使，兩蕃、勃海、黑水四府經略使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yimou, Lushan was made Prefect of Yingzhou, commander of the Pinglu Army, and commissioner over Liaofan, Bohai, and Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yimou, An Lushan was made prefect of Yingzhou, commander of the Pinglu Army, and commissioner over Liaofan, Bohai, and Heishui.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙申，上幸驪山温泉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，分北庭、安西爲二節度。

translations.literal: On renyin Beiting and Anxi were divided into two separate commands.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Beiting and Anxi were split into two military commands.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚戌，司空邠王守禮薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Minister of Works Prince of Bin Shouli died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Minister of Works Prince of Bin Shouli died.

sentences.zh: 守禮庸鄙無-{才}-識，毎天將雨及霽，守禮必先言之，已而皆驗。

translations.literal: Shouli was vulgar and without talent or insight; whenever rain or clearing was due, Shouli would always speak of it first, and afterward it always proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bin, Shouli, was coarse and untalented; before every rain or clearing he would announce it first—and he was always right.

sentences.zh: 岐、薛諸王言-{於}-上曰：「邠兄有-{術}-。」

translations.literal: The princes of Qi and Xue said to the Emperor: "Elder Brother Bin has arts."
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Qi and Xue told the Emperor: "Our elder brother Bin has occult skill."

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「臣無-{術}-。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Your subject has no arts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked why; he answered: "I have no occult arts.

sentences.zh: 則天時以章懷之故，幽閉宮中十-{餘}-年，歳賜敕杖者數四，背瘢甚厚，將雨則沉悶，將霽則輕爽，臣以此知之耳。」

translations.literal: Because of Zhanghuai, Heaven's seasons confined me in the palace more than ten years; several times a year imperial cane was bestowed, and the scars on my back are very thick—when rain is coming they grow heavy and dull, when clearing is coming they grow light and fresh; your subject knew it from this alone.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhanghuai's sake I was shut in the palace more than ten years; the throne sent the disciplinary cane several times a year, and the welts on my back are deep—before rain they ache and weigh on me, before clearing they ease; I knew the weather only from that.

sentences.zh: 因流涕沾襟；

translations.literal: Thereupon tears soaked his robe;
translations.idiomatic: Tears then soaked the front of his robe;

sentences.zh: 上亦爲之慘然。

translations.literal: the Emperor too was deeply saddened.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor was deeply moved as well.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上還宮。

translations.literal: On xinyou the Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Emperor Xuanzong returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛未，太尉-{寧}-王憲薨。

translations.literal: On xinwei Grand Preceptor Prince Ning, Xian, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Grand Preceptor Prince Ning, Li Xian, died.

sentences.zh: 上哀惋特甚，曰：「天下，兄之天下也；

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned with exceptional grief and said: "The realm was elder brother's realm;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved exceedingly and said: "The realm was my brother's realm;

sentences.zh: 兄固讓-{於}-我，爲唐太伯，常名不足以處之。」

translations.literal: elder brother firmly yielded it to me, becoming Tang's Taibo—ordinary titles are not enough to contain him.
translations.idiomatic: my brother firmly yielded it to me, the Taibo of Tang—no ordinary title can do him justice.

sentences.zh: 乃謚曰讓皇帝。

translations.literal: He was therefore given the posthumous title Emperor Rang.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore posthumously styled Emperor Rang.

sentences.zh: 其子汝陽王璡，上表追述先-{志}-謙-{沖}-，不敢當帝號；

translations.literal: His son Prince Ru of Yang, Jin, memorialized tracing his late father's intent of humility and restraint, not daring to bear an emperor's title;
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Ru of Yang, Li Jin, memorialized that his father's intent had been humility and that the family dared not accept an imperial title;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 敛日，内出服，以手書致-{於}-靈座，書稱「隆基白」；

translations.literal: On the day of encoffining, mourning garments were sent from within the palace; the Emperor wrote by his own hand and placed it before the bier, signing "Bai from Longji";
translations.idiomatic: On the day of encoffining, mourning dress came from within the palace; the Emperor wrote in his own hand to the spirit seat, signing "From Longji";

sentences.zh: 又名其墓曰惠陵，追謚其妃元氏曰恭皇-{后}-，附葬焉。

translations.literal: he also named the tomb Huiling, posthumously styled his consort the Yuan clan as Empress Gonghuang, and buried her there with him.
translations.idiomatic: he named the tomb Huiling, posthumously ennobled his consort Lady Yuan as Empress Gonghuang, and buried her beside him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙巳，吐蕃屠達化縣，陷石堡城，蓋嘉運不能-{御}-。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yisi, Tibet massacred Dahua County and took Shibao Fort; Gai Jiayun could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yisi, Tibet slaughtered Dahua County and captured Shibao Fort; Gai Jiayun could not hold them off.
